name: Dammërstein
introduction:
Dammërstein, the Stone House

In 1115 five magi raised a house of grey stone on a granite spur above the Schattenbach, in the southern Black Forest. A Bonisagus, a Criamon, a Tytalus, a Merinita and a Tremere: they kept to themselves so well that the Rhine Tribunal half forgot them. For ninety years they added cellars and galleries into the hill, gathered vis from the Faerie well, the old firs, the mountain tarn and the Roman watchtower on the ridge, and worked in the black glass under the cliff.

Then the harvests stopped. The household drifted down the valley, the pacts with the forest's folk lapsed, and by 1211 the Founders were gone. Only Kyrillos of Criamon remains, barefoot in the halls under the manor, and he says little.

Now word of the place is moving again. Letters in the archive at Durenmar speak of a spell that held more vis than its Art allows. A Redcap tells of Vim silk sold at a Tribunal fair. A scrap of an older faith names a place "where the glass drinks the gods' gifts". All of it points up the Schattenbach.

The saga opens in Spring 1220, as a new company of magi comes to claim a house that is half sealed: doors closed with wax, a library of the Founders' books, a laboratory of volcanic glass, a faerie court owed old debts, and a baron down the valley who has noticed the lights on the spur again.

What the pack holds: the covenant of Dammërstein (Medium, 450 Build Points), its Founders and household, its library and devices, the places and neighbours of the upper Schattenbach, seven creatures and nine calendar entries. Choosing it brings in the Rhine Tribunal, from Guardians of the Forests, first.

covenants.name: Dammërstein
covenants.notes:
The Stone House stands on a granite spur above the Schattenbach: a manor and bailey of grey stone that the Founders kept adding to for ninety years, until its cellars and galleries ran back into the hill. Its round tower holds the Founders' library, with Kyrillos's observatory under the ring of windows at the top. In the cliff below, a pillared front older than Rome stands around a door of black glass, and on the ridge above, the Roman watchtower keeps its watch over nothing. Much of the house is still shut: doors sealed with wax, roofs fallen in, stairs that were not there yesterday.

For a decade only Kyrillos of Criamon lived here, barefoot in the Echoing Halls under the manor and rarely seen outside them, with Gertrud the cook, her deaf husband Kuno and their grandchildren, who stayed when everyone else went down the valley. The gate stands ready to open again. Whoever comes up the Schattenbach will find the forge cold, the gatehouse empty and the stewardship nobody's, and Sigismund already at work copying and binding what the library still holds. Lutz and his sons bring stores up from the Kinzig valley twice a season.

Below the spur, the charcoal-burners of Kohlergrund still pay their rent to the Stone House, as they did all the years the lights were out, and leave bread at the gate while they wait to see what kind of master has come. They are not the only ones watching.

inhabitants.name: Gertrud and the old household
inhabitants.description: Gertrud the cook, her deaf husband Kuno and their grandchildren, who stayed with Kyrillos when the others left.

inhabitants.name: Lutz and sons
inhabitants.description: Brings stores up from the Kinzig valley twice a season.

possessions.name: Hochtannen resin
possessions.description: The eldest seven silver firs of the Hochtannen, Abnoba's grove, weep it at midsummer: 3 pawns a year, 2 of them from the eldest. Take it by hand, never with iron, never by cutting the bark (the Hochtannen's card has the rule). Mother Agathe gathers it and keeps one pawn in three. If the eldest fall, the yield is 1 pawn.

possessions.name: Mirror Tarn reflections
possessions.description: At the spring equinox, clear panes laid on the Mirror Tarn lift its reflections away: 3 pawns of Imaginem, one to a pane, lifted with no face over the water. Four of Matthaios's panes are left in the Founders' tower. Never lift your own face, and never look too long (the Mirror Tarn's card).

possessions.name: Abnoba inscriptions
possessions.description: The Latin letters to Abnoba on the tower's inner walls weep a clear resin each winter: 2 pawns of Intellego. Burn the first drop on the altar at the solstice, with the watchword, as her due; that keeps the serpent asleep. Left ungathered, the resin drips into the serpent's pool.

possessions.name: What the Founders left in the stores
possessions.physical_form: Three old skeins of well silk, gone grey

income_sources.name: Rents of the Kohlergrund
income_sources.description: Coin and charcoal from the hamlet in the valley below, paid for as long as anyone remembers, and paid still.

income_sources.name: Kyrillos's testimony
income_sources.description: Fees from magi who come, or send, to Kyrillos to learn what really happened to a thing, a book or a place.

diary.name: The Spinner's Court: an old pact, unpaid
diary.details: The Court is Wary of the Stone House. The silk pact passes with the house, and so do its arrears: about eighty secrets owed since 1200. Renewing the pact means settling, or bargaining down, that debt.

diary.name: The Whispering Well silk
diary.details: Four pawns of Vim a year, spun on the webs since 1200 and taken only at the Spinner's pleasure. Every skein the covenant takes is Might she cannot spend, so she will want the pact renewed on her terms.

diary.name: Hildegund's faerie bargains
diary.details: The Court still owes Hildegund's three favours, 80, 80 and 90 Build Points, and by her own law the Spinner must honour them. She won't mention them. The covenant must first learn they exist: from Bargains with the Spinner, from Mother Agathe, or from Kyrillos.

diary.name: The serpent under the Watchtower
diary.details: The resin has gone ungathered since 1211 and pooled in the cellar. This winter the pool reaches the serpent's Might, and it will drink unless the resin is gathered and the pool drained before the solstice. Burning Abnoba's due at the solstice (the first drop, with the watchword) keeps it asleep even then.

diary.name: The watch on the ridge
diary.details: A legionary keeps watch on the ridge on winter nights. He challenges those who climb to the tower, and wants to be relieved of his post.

diary.name: The baron's axes
diary.details: Wolfram von Schattenbach's loggers make camp at the valley mouth this summer. His grandfather's grant gives him the timber of the whole valley, and Kalb of Strassburg wants the Hochtannen as beams. If the eldest firs fall, the resin gives 1 pawn a year, not 3.

diary.name: Kohlergrund pays twice
diary.details: The burners pay the baron a forest penny and the Stone House its rent, and can't go on paying both. Before winter is out they will stop paying whichever master looks weaker.

diary.name: Mother Agathe's silence
diary.details: The wise woman at the head of the valley thinks the Stone House owes her for forty years of silence. She knows something about the old pact she cannot say, and she would give a great deal to see Hildegund home.

diary.name: The warden outside the gate
diary.details: Ilona of Tremere, the Founders' warden, has lived outside Coeris since 1212: she cannot cross a threshold uninvited, and Benedek will not invite her in. No one at the Stone House has invited her home, which is why the valley's wards lapsed. A letter from the new council, worded as an invitation, would bring her back, and she would want to know first whether Nikephoros is alive. He is at the Cave of Twisting Shadows, and if he comes north he will test the wards to see whether she is back. Bringing the two of them together again is a story the covenant could give them (Ilona's card has the whole of it).

covenants.summary: The Stone House, in the southern Black Forest. Its Founders kept so much to themselves that the Tribunal half forgot them, and for a decade no light has shown on the spur. Now letters, a Redcap's story and a scrap of an older faith have begun to point up the Schattenbach again, to the black glass under the cliff, and to the house that stands empty above it.
covenants.what_matters: Original research into vis, and what the Founders left behind.

charter_of_covenant.name: The Founders' Covenant Accord
charter_of_covenant.preamble:
Be it known to all who read this Accord, that in the spring of the year of Our Lord eleven hundred and fifteen, upon the spur above the Schattenbach, five magi of the Order of Hermes laid the seven foundation stones of this house, and swore upon them as here follows.

Ἐπὶ τούτοις τοῖς λίθοις οἰκοδομοῦμεν. (Upon these stones we build.)

I, [name], magus of the Order of Hermes, of the House of [House], do swear upon these seven stones, which lie beneath this house as the work we intend shall lie beneath our lives:

That I shall hold the Oath of Hermes above this Accord, and this Accord above every other bond.

That what this house finds, I shall share; what this house keeps, I shall keep; and what this house hides, I shall hide.

That I shall not turn my Art against any who seal with me, nor suffer another so to do while I may prevent it.

That I shall sit in the council of this house as one voice among equals, and shall answer for this Accord to that council and to no other.

Ὃ μόνοι οὐ δυνάμεθα, ὁμοῦ δυνάμεθα. Quod singuli nequimus, una possumus.

Thus sworn by Matthaios of Bonisagus, Kyrillos of Criamon, Nikephoros of Tytalus, Ilona of Tremere and Hildegund of Merinita, each with a hand upon the stones, and set down by Ilona, warden. So mote it be. Γένοιτο.

clauses.text: Be it known that the sodales of this house are the five who have sworn upon its stones. Another magus may be admitted a sodalis by the council, and shall swear this oath upon the stones before it.

Any sodalis may give a guest the shelter of this house, upon that sodalis's word and at that sodalis's charge. A guest shall have bread, a bed and the protection of the house, and no voice in council. The sodalis who gave it, or the council, may withdraw it.
A Founder who leaves takes only what is theirs, and their quarters are sealed until the council opens them.
clauses.note: Why the Founders' quarters are sealed still.

clauses.text: The house decides in council, each Founder one voice. The warden keeps the accord and the keys of the sealed quarters, and calls the council.

The council shall sit at each solstice and each equinox, in the hall beneath the tower, and no voice in it shall weigh more than another. A matter touching the Crucible, the silk pact or the sealed quarters shall require every voice; any other matter, three.
What any of the five finds here, under the hill, in the Crucible or in the forest, is shared with all five.
clauses.note: Kyrillos, and the stone in the lowest gallery.

clauses.text: What each sodalis brought to this house, and what each shall write, is their own, and the house shall claim no part of it.
Each sodalis shall have quarters, a laboratory, bread and fire, and free use of the books of the tower.
Nothing of the house goes to the Tribunal, to any House or to any covenant without the consent of all five.
clauses.note: Matthaios's thirty years of letters to Durenmar. Ilona never scored it for herself, though Coeris asked her for thirty years.

clauses.text: The house deals with the Spinner's people through Hildegund alone, and the pact's secrets are paid by the house, each Founder giving in turn.
Each sodalis shall take a turn at the harvests and at the keeping of the wards, as the warden shall set them.

A sodalis who breaks this Accord shall answer for it to the council, which may withhold the books and vis of the house until amends are made. No matter of this Accord shall be carried to any Tribunal. So mote it be.

covenants.secrets:
Why it fell. The Founders came for different things: Matthaios for the Deeper Vessel, Kyrillos for what lies under the hill, Hildegund for the Spinner's court, Nikephoros for the contest, and Ilona because Coeris sent her. Three things broke them, together: jealousy (of Matthaios's Crucible and the claim House Bonisagus might make on its results, and of what Kyrillos kept to himself), pressure from Coeris on Ilona, and ninety years without a result. Trust broke around 1200; after that the vis went unharvested, the pacts lapsed and the household drifted away, until a last quarrel in 1211. The Founders' fates are known only to Kyrillos, and he has his own agenda.

Hidden Resources (250 Build Points each, not yet found):

Matthaios's sealed study, off the Echoing Halls: his journal of the Deeper Vessel (about 30 of 45 breakthrough points), the insight Lab Texts of his two stabilized Discoveries, which another magus may study a season each to gain the same insight, and an Art Summa on Vim (Level 16, Quality 12).

The sealed Founders' quarters, in the oldest part of the manor: each Founder's personal books (among them Ilona's Rego summa The Rule of the Hand, Level 10, Quality 10, and Nikephoros's Mentem summa Of Minds and Their Doors, Level 10, Quality 9), a store of mixed vis that was once Nikephoros's cache, and Nikephoros's Mirror of Contest, which turns a spell of up to the 30th level back on its caster (on his card, under Enchanted Devices, until it is found). Ilona's letters with Benedek of Tremere are there too, as story, not counted in the 250.

Hildegund's faerie bargains: three favours the Spinner's Court owes, and her talisman, a silver spindle, hidden in the manor's chapel (on Hildegund's card, under Enchanted Devices, until it is found). The 250 Build Points are split 80, 80 and 90. When a favour is called in, choose what it buys at the Covenants creation costs: vis stores at 1 Build Point per 5 pawns (faerie-spun Vim silk suits it best), an enchanted effect worked by the faeries at 2 Build Points per 5 levels, books on Faerie Lore or Vim, or a season of faerie labour or protection. Calling one in costs the Spinner's price, a secret, and is a natural moment for the Faerie Court Hook to stir. Spinning a thread with the spindle at the Wheel brings Hildegund back to herself: she knows the year and what she is, and can bargain again. Only she can call in the third favour (the 90), the half-made one whose price was never named. She still cannot leave until the arrears are paid (see Settling the arrears, below, and the Court's page). The magi must first learn the bargains exist: from Bargains with the Spinner in the library, from Mother Agathe, or from Kyrillos. (The split, the price and the spindle's rule are this pack's design; Covenants gives only the 250 Build Points.)

The legionaries' pay-chest is the serpent's hoard: a story reward, not Build Points.

The Founders' charter. In 1115 Duke Berthold III of Zähringen granted "the spur above the Schattenbach and the valley from the narrows to the springs, with its waters, its land and its people" to the house that stands on the spur, through a Strassburg notary in Nikephoros's pay. It is the reason Kohlergrund has paid its rent to the Stone House ever since. The sealed copy lies in the Founders' sealed quarters. With the Zähringen gone it is only worth what their heir will confirm: the Emperor's Schultheiss at Offenburg could confirm it, and it would take a story to get him to, not a spell.

Settling the arrears. The pact's arrears are about eighty secrets, one for each skein spun since 1200, and Hildegund is their surety. There are four ways to settle them. (1) Pay them, secret by secret. (2) Bargain them down to great secrets, as in 1180, when one great skein was paid for with a single great secret. A great secret stands for five years of skeins, so four of them would clear the arrears. It is the same five years for which the app secures a Contested Resource, so a great secret paid now also secures the silk for five years. (3) Call in one of Hildegund's first two favours to clear the house's account. They were bargained "for the house", so under her first law the Spinner must honour it. It spends 80 Build Points of this Boon, and calling it in still costs her price, a secret. She will settle no more than the words say, so they must name it exactly: "the arrears of the silk pact, to the last skein". (4) If Hildegund is woken, she can finish the third favour by naming its price as the arrears, and so pay for her own freedom. The Spinner will fight this hardest of all, because it gives her nothing she wants.

tribunals.name: The Rhine Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The First Tribunal covers every Imperial land north of the Alps: from the Jutland border in the north to the Danube in the south, and from the mouth of the Schelde, the Ardennes and the Argonne in the west to the Oder in the east, where its border with the Novgorod Tribunal is disputed and shifts. About 130 magi, close to a ninth of the Order, make it the largest and oldest of the thirteen Tribunals; it hosts the Grand Tribunal, and the domus magnae of Bonisagus (Durenmar), Bjornaer (Crintera) and Merinita (Irencillia) all stand in its forests. Its magi descend from Roman and Germanic traditions with Slavic and Scandinavian additions, and about a sixth of them are peregrinatores, wandering magi who guest at covenants under the Tribunal's old laws of hospitality.

The Tribunal meets every seven years at Durenmar, opening on Walpurgis Night, the eve of the first of May, and sitting for over a week; the gilds and some Houses meet in the three days before. Its Praeco is not its oldest magus but the Prima of House Bonisagus, who votes the sigil of Bonisagus by proxy, a custom since Notatus; some, led by Fengheld, now want the Order's usual rule instead. Magi hold the ranks of journeyman, master and archmage: only masters take apprentices and hold a retired magus's sigil by proxy, archmagi hold two, and in a dispute that certamen would otherwise settle the higher rank has the right. Every apprentice trained here spends a season at Durenmar under a Bonisagus, and most join one of the six political gilds, which transcend House and covenant and monopolise the Tribunal's long-term quarrels, so that little changes at its meetings.

The Rhine is no longer a leading force in the Order but is respected for its age and cannot be ignored for its size. Its old tension with Novgorod continues except among the Bjornaer; the Greater Alps are friendly trading neighbours who think their Roman covenants superior; Transylvania's Tremere press on Moravia. The next meeting is in 1221, the 1360th year of the Aegis.
tribunals.history:
Roman Germania. Rome's frontier ran along the Rhine and the Danube, and under Domitian the gap between the rivers was closed by the limes, a fortified line from near Remagen to Abusina above Regensburg. West of the Rhine the provinces of Upper and Lower Germania had cities like Cologne, Bonn, Trier and Mainz, with forum, baths and temples, where the priests of Mercury were everywhere. Beyond the river lay Germania Magna, forest, moor and fen, whose tribes of hunters, herders and small farmers worshipped Woden, Thunor, Tius and Fria. Rome never held it: in 9 AD Hermann of the Cherusci destroyed three legions under Varus in the Teutoburger Forest. Tacitus, about 98 AD, found the Germans brave, honest and hospitable but greedy, rough and fond of drink. By the third century the limes was abandoned under pressure from Franks, Alemanni and Goths, though Trier flourished as a western imperial capital under Constantine early in the fourth.

The Great Migration and the Merovingians. The wandering of the peoples was a slow drift rather than a flood: Goths into Gaul and Iberia, Vandals into Italy, Burgundians to the land that bears their name and to Worms in 413, Alemanni over the Rhine, Saxons, Angles and Jutes to Britain. The one violent eruption was Attila's Huns, checked at Chalons in 451 by Merovech and the Roman general Aetius. By about 600 the movements had ended, Slavs filling the empty lands of the Vistula and Oder and Saxons, Swabians, Frisians and Bavarians settled between the old Roman lines and the Slavs. The Franks rose under the Merovingians, named for the half-magical chieftain Merovech, whose grandson Clovis was baptised, united the Franks and ruled from Paris. The dynasty, credited with miraculous gifts, decayed after Clovis's grandsons Sigebert and Chilperic split the kingdom, and by 687 the mayors of the palace ruled in all but name. In 751 Pepin the Short sent the last Merovingian to a monastery and took the crown with the Church's blessing.

The Franks and Charlemagne. Charlemagne, king of the Franks from 768, carried Frankish rule, bishops and learning eastward from Aachen in three decisive campaigns that reached the Elbe and the Danube, gave the pagan Saxons the choice of baptism or death and planted bishoprics from Hamburg and Bremen to Paderborn, Hildesheim and Halberstadt. He fostered schools, made the count palatine his chief justice and in 789 outlawed sorcery and paganism while tolerating benevolent magic. On Christmas Day 800 the Pope crowned him emperor in Rome, and at his death in 814 the Frankish Empire held everything south and west of the Elbe, Bavaria included. His son Louis the Pious fought his own sons, and Frankish custom divided the inheritance: the Treaty of Verdun in 843 gave the west to Charles the Bald, the east to Louis the German and the imperial title with a narrow middle strip to Lothar. The later Carolingians faced Norse raids and the deposition of Charles the Fat in 887, and the last of them to be emperor, Arnulf of Carinthia, died in 899 amid rumours of murder.

The Ottonians. The heirs of Louis the German were nominal kings over Saxons, Swabians, Bavarians, Burgundians and Franconians while Moslems raided Italy, Northmen the coasts and Magyar horsemen plundered as far as France. The Magyar threat rallied the tribes behind Henry the Fowler, duke of Saxony, crowned in 919, who crushed the Magyars at Riade on the Unstrut in 933; his son Otto, crowned at Aachen in 936, ended the menace for good at the Lechfeld in 955. Otto's imperial coronation in Rome in 962 bound the German kings, henceforth emperors, to Italian politics for good. Under the four Saxon emperors the empire became the leading power west of the Adriatic, Slavs and Danes were converted and bishoprics founded in the Eastern Marches and Denmark, while some pagan Slavs withdrew to Rügen. Each Ottonian left exactly one heir, which spared the empire the Frankish habit of partition. Bishops became the emperor's instruments of government, invested by him with spiritual and secular office alike, a practice soon to be contested.

The Salians and the Investiture Contest. Conrad II began the Salian line in 1024, reaffirmed single inheritance of the crown, won in Italy and added the Burgundian crown in 1033; in 1037 the unfree knights called ministeriales entered the German feudal order. Henry III secured the loyalty of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary. Then in 1075 a papal bull forbade laymen to invest prelates, opening five decades of struggle over who led the Church: Gregory VII excommunicated Henry IV and forced his penance at Canossa in 1077, though Henry was crowned emperor in Rome in 1084 all the same. Papal authority advanced with the First Crusade, during which crusaders massacred the Jews of Worms, Speyer, Cologne, Trier and Mainz in 1096 while Henry tried in vain to punish them. The quarrel ended at Worms in 1122: the Church would elect its own bishops and abbots, while the emperor might attend elections and invest German prelates with their secular honours, keeping their feudal dues and much real influence. Henry V, the last Salian, died in 1125.

The Hohenstaufen and Frederick Barbarossa. Lothar II's narrow election in 1125 and the Swabians' choice of Conrad III as anti-king in 1127 began the long feud of Welf and Hohenstaufen; Conrad became king in 1137 and his nephew Frederick Barbarossa followed in 1152. Barbarossa spent a third of his reign in Italy, where the towns resisted royal dues: the Milanese beat him at Legnano in 1176, the Helvetians held out and plague struck his army before Rome. In Germany his contest with Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony and leader of the Welfs, ended in 1180 with the duchy broken up, Henry exiled, Bavaria given to Otto of Wittelsbach and the Saxon lands to Hohenstaufen men. From about 1140 the push to the east cleared forests and planted settlers, a concern of frontier princes more than kings, who still looked to the Rhineland and Italy for the profits of lordship. Frederick carried the relics of the Three Magi from Milan to Cologne in 1164 and drowned in 1190 crossing the Seleph on crusade. His son Henry VI conquered Sicily in 1194 and died after six years; rival kings Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick were elected in 1198, Philip was murdered at Bamberg in 1208, and the Welf Otto IV, crowned in Rome in 1209, was excommunicated and deposed.

The empire in 1220. Frederick II, of a German father and a Sicilian mother, was made king of Germany in 1212 and crowned at Aachen in 1214, helped Philip of France crush Otto IV at Bouvines that year, and was crowned emperor in Rome in 1220 after vowing a crusade he has made no move to begin. He prefers Sicily and a court of brilliant minds, writes poetry and a treatise on falconry, is called the wonder of the world, and has taken the wizard Michael Scot into his service, to the Church's unease. Germany is a loose elective kingdom with no capital: the king is crowned at Aachen and keeps his treasury at Nuremberg, and the princely nobility of dukes, archbishops, prince-bishops, landgraves, margraves and counts attend the Diet and choose him. Fiefs pass only in the male line and are divided among sons, so the provinces have splintered into countless small lordships, with new estates carved from eastern colonisation, forest clearance and drained marsh. Most cities belong to counts, dukes or bishops, but fourteen Free Imperial Cities answer only to the emperor. The Zähringen dukes died out in 1218, the Teutonic Knights and the Sword Brothers crusade in the Baltic, and Valdemar II of Denmark holds Holstein. More than half the land is still forest, and magic has withdrawn from the swelling cities into the woods.
tribunals.meeting_place: Durenmar, in the Black Forest: the Forum of Hermes and the Tribunal Field

cases.title: Heorot asks to join the Tribunal
cases.charge: Heorot, founded on Zealand in 1215 with Oculus Septentrionalis' backing, applies for membership at the Tribunal of 1221; Zealand is nominally Novgorod's, which does not know of it.

cases.title: The Lusatia chapter and the Novgorod border
cases.charge: Fengheld's Lusatia chapter house stands ten miles from the agreed border, the latest of the Rhine's boundary disputes with Novgorod; the Tribunal is asked to assert its claim east to the Oder and to take the matter to the Grand Tribunal of 1228.

cases.title: Choosing the Praeco by age
cases.charge: That the Rhine should choose its Praeco as the rest of the Order does, by age, and not always the Prima of Bonisagus; Eule of Fengheld would then be the likeliest, with Caecilius of Durenmar and Schadrit of Dankmar the other candidates.

cases.title: Crintera and the Danes
cases.charge: Fifty years after Valdemar's invasion of Rügen, Crintera again asks the Tribunal to act against the Danish occupation and the Dominion it brings; the Tribunal split on gild lines in 1186 and Caecilius ruled against in 1194, and Bjornaer who attacked settlers have been prosecuted since.

cases.title: Triamore's dealings with mundanes
cases.charge: Triamore's long entanglement in the politics of the Meuse, for which the Quaesitores have sought censure for years; Daria la Gris has so far talked the covenant out of it.

cases.title: Fengheld's house at Durenmar
cases.charge: Fengheld is building a three-storey stone house on the Tribunal Field as a permanent chapter at Durenmar, with a laboratory and its own Mercere Portal, after Durenmar refused it a Portal in the Forum; Durenmar calls it an encroachment.

cases.title: Waddenzee's piracy
cases.charge: Waddenzee's magi prey on North Sea shipping; the Quaesitores have warned them repeatedly that they walk a fine line and will get no help if the mundane powers move against them, and that each would face High Crimes charges.

cases.title: Odorpes of Fengheld's neglect
cases.charge: Fengheld has more than once accused its own Odorpes, of the Lusatia chapter, of neglecting her duties to the covenant.

cases.title: The Rhine Gorge after the ban
cases.charge: The twenty-year ban on magic in the Rhine Gorge runs out in 1220; whoever would found a covenant there needs a sponsor from every covenant. Durenmar wants a neutral, traditional foundation; Fengheld would rather it were one of its chapters.

rulings.title: A season at Durenmar
rulings.says: From the Tribunal's founding: every apprentice trained in the Rhine spends at least one season at Durenmar, taught by a magus of House Bonisagus.

rulings.title: The laws of hospitality (961 AA)
rulings.says: A magus may ask hospitality of any lawful Rhine covenant, which must publish its conditions; a guest who accepts them is guaranteed at least three and at most seven years, pays at least three pawns of vis a year, and the conditions are the same for every guest in residence and change only when there are none.

rulings.title: Proxy sigils (1017 AA)
rulings.says: Firm rules on the voting of retired magi, ending twenty years of dispute: a master is entrusted with one retired magus's sigil, an archmage with a second, cast in the retired magus's name and, by custom, by his likely wishes.

rulings.title: Ranks
rulings.says: Only a master may take an apprentice (a journeyman's filius is treated as a new hedge recruit); three masters of other covenants, Houses and gilds confer the rank; in any dispute certamen would otherwise settle, the higher rank has the right. House Tremere contests this, as it was made to curb them.

rulings.title: Founding a covenant (1024 AA)
rulings.says: A new covenant needs a sponsoring magus from every existing covenant of the Tribunal. Arae Flaviae and Schwarzburg abolished the same year. Chapter houses need no such leave, which is how Fengheld grows.

rulings.title: Guardians of the Forests (1192 AA)
rulings.says: Magi may actively defend the wilderness against those who would destroy it. In 1194 Caecilius ruled that the Danish occupation of Rügen is no such destruction, as no wilderness was invaded.

rulings.title: A day's march (1248 AA)
rulings.says: A magical site within a day's march of a covenant belongs to it; Valdus of Tytalus, who harvested Treverorum's, was fined a pawn as the covenant had lost nothing, and told to ask in future.

rulings.title: A covenant without a site
rulings.says: At the Ash Gild's urging the Tribunal founded Oculus Septentrionalis to learn of the Norse wizards, ruling that a covenant needs no site at founding, only magi bound by a charter. In 1158 its magi were fined three pawns each for keeping neither.

rulings.title: Dankmar against Durenmar
rulings.says: Durenmar, found to have molested the fay and plundered faerie sites, paid a rook of vis to every other covenant and was barred from faerie sites for fourteen years unless it made peace with them.

rulings.title: No magic in the Rhine Gorge (1339 AA)
rulings.says: After Rheinstein was destroyed by the archbishop of Trier's army, largely through its own doing, no magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years: a ban that ends in 1220.

rulings.title: Waddenzee is Terschelling
rulings.says: The two survivors of Terschelling renamed it Waddenzee with a new charter and symbol; a vote to call it a new covenant needing leave failed, by the Oak and Ash Gilds. The same year Rethra, silent for decades, was declared abolished.

diary.title: Mercurian temple at Durenmar's site
diary.details: Priests of the Roman Cult of Mercury raise a temple deep in the Black Forest, on the ground Durenmar later takes, hoping to turn the primeval power of the Hercynian Forest to their own use. In the Roman years they bind the forest's spirit by its own oaths into what is now the Fane of the Founders; a wild splinter of it escapes south and in time becomes the King of the Black Mountain.

diary.title: Black Forest Road finished
diary.details: The Eighth Legion under Cornelius Clemens completes the road from Offenburg to Rottweil with the help of Mercurian priests, who set warding milestones along it. The Roman limes of the same age cuts the Black Forest, and its spirit, off from the rest of the Hercynian Forest.

diary.title: Donar Oak felled
diary.details: St Boniface cuts down the Donar Oak at Geismar in Thuringia and builds an oratory of St Peter from its wood. Pagan magic, relics and belief wane from that day, and the one great spirit of the Hercynian Forest is shattered into the many lesser forests of Germany.

diary.title: Trianoma apprenticed to Bonisagus
diary.details: Trianoma finds Bonisagus in his cave in the Alps, becomes his apprentice and learns the Parma Magica.

diary.title: The Founders gathered
diary.details: From 731 to 767 Trianoma seeks out the wizards who will be the Founders and brings them to Bonisagus, who refines his theory with each. Merinita comes in from the wild and persuades the shapeshifter Bjornaer to join, for which Bjornaer's old fellows, the sorceress Gyongy among them, condemn her.

diary.title: Bonisagus settles at Durenmar
diary.details: Bonisagus leaves his Alpine cave for the ruined Roman temple in the Black Forest, hoping to reconcile his Hermetic theory with the forest's primeval magic; between 754 and 767 the place is built up with room for many magi.

diary.title: Order of Hermes founded at Durenmar
diary.details: The Founders compose and swear the Oath at the Fane of the Founders and hold the first Tribunal gathering. Bonisagus's followers and some of the Founders settle at Durenmar and build the covenant.

diary.title: Covenants on Durenmar's model
diary.details: Between 767 and 773 Flambeau and his apprentices leave to found Val-Negra in the Pyrenees, and other magi found covenants of their own after Durenmar's pattern.

diary.title: Bjornaer's first council on Rügen
diary.details: Bjornaer and her followers meet in council on Rügen; her House has gathered there every twelve years since.

diary.title: Second Grand Tribunal
diary.details: A Tribunal is ruled to need at least twelve magi from four covenants. Crintera, the domus magna of House Bjornaer, and Fenistal, the domus magna of House Merinita, are founded.

diary.title: First Rhine Tribunal (919 AA)
diary.details: The Rhine Tribunal meets for the first time, at Durenmar. Arae Flaviae in Swabia and Rethra in the Eastern Marches are founded.

diary.title: Jerbiton before Charlemagne
diary.details: Jerbiton, who has taken on the apprentices of the imperial mage-smith Carolinus, meets Charlemagne. The emperor outlaws sorcery and paganism but allows the kind of benevolent magic Jerbiton practises.

diary.title: Merinita leaves the Order
diary.details: The Founder Merinita is seen for the last time, going to seek the spirit of the wilderness; the Bohemian chapter dates her going to 785 and says her last words are carved over Irencillia's gate. Fenistal becomes the first covenant to enter Winter, and the new Primus Quendalon founds Irencillia.

diary.title: Third Grand Tribunal
diary.details: After the gathering Quendalon goes into the faerie woods of Bohemia, leaving Myanar to lead House Merinita.

diary.title: Quendalon returns; Irencillia the domus magna
diary.details: In 801 and 802 Quendalon comes back from the faerie woods and Myanar denies he is the true Quendalon. The struggle kills Myanar and loses Fenistal; Irencillia becomes the domus magna of House Merinita, the House turns to faerie magic, and the Elder Gild splits away from the Hawthorn Gild.

diary.title: Tytalus lost in the Maddenhofen Woods
diary.details: The Founder Tytalus enters the Maddenhofen Woods in Bohemia, saying he will face the Queen of all the Fae, and is never seen again.

diary.title: Bjornaer's last words
diary.details: At the Gathering of Twelve Years at Crintera, Bjornaer speaks for the last time to her House and goes into the forest as a bear.

diary.title: Fifth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Grand Tribunals are to meet every thirty-three years from now on, and the regional Tribunals every seven years from 836.

diary.title: Hercynius's lineage
diary.details: From about 850 to 948 Hercynius of Bonisagus founds a lineage within his House and draws other magi to his teaching on the forest's magic.

diary.title: Tribunal of 996 AA: the Twilight spirits
diary.details: The spirits of three magi lost to Twilight famously return to the gathering.

diary.title: Sixth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The borders of the Tribunals are fixed along the lines of the Frankish partition and named: Rhine, Normandy, Provencal, Britannian, Roman, Theban, Eastern and Greater Alps.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1017 AA: proxy sigils
diary.details: Firm rules on the votes of retired magi end twenty years of dispute over whether and how their sigils may be cast.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1024 AA: founding rules
diary.details: Arae Flaviae and Schwarzburg are abolished, and strict rules for the founding of new covenants are agreed.

diary.title: Rudiaria founded (1031 AA)
diary.details: The Tribunal sponsors Rudiaria, a Flambeau-leaning covenant on the right bank of the Rhine opposite Bingen, and grants it every magical site along the river between Mainz and Cologne.

diary.title: Sirmium destroyed by the Magyars
diary.details: Magyar raiders destroy the covenant of Sirmium in Meissen, and with it the region's known vis sources. Wiederich of Flambeau, the only survivor, joins Henry the Fowler's army for revenge and serves at Riade in 933 and on the Lech in 955; after the Magyars' defeat House Bjornaer adopts three Magyar shapechangers, whose horse-hearted line survives, and Wiederich's descendants have hounded them as blood enemies ever since.

diary.title: Oakdell founded (1073 AA)
diary.details: Diedne magi found Oakdell in the Westerwald, a dozen miles east of the Rhine, with the Tribunal's sponsorship and on condition that it keeps out of Rudiaria's territory (the book's list of covenants puts its founding in 931).

diary.title: Tribunal of 1080 AA: the Rowan Gild
diary.details: The Tribunal's followers of Diedne, until now of the Hawthorn Gild, found the Rowan Gild.

diary.title: Diabolism charge against Eginolf (1101 AA)
diary.details: Charges of diabolism against Eginolf of Flambeau of Rudiaria are not proven, but the reports of malefic doings near the covenant are noted with disapproval; Rudiaria is ordered to investigate, report within seven years and stop troubling the mundanes.

diary.title: Rudiaria destroyed (1108 AA)
diary.details: House Mercere reports Rudiaria burnt out in what looks like a catastrophic magical accident, every magus slain or missing; diabolism is suspected. The fall comes with a crippling famine and unrest in the region.

diary.title: Rudiaria's site sanctified (1115 AA)
diary.details: Nothing can be salvaged at Rudiaria; an archbishop of Mainz has sanctified the ground. Oakdell's claim to Rudiaria's sites is refused.

diary.title: Waldherz founded
diary.details: Followers of Hercynius leave Durenmar to found Waldherz, first as a chapter house and later as a disputed covenant in its own right.

diary.title: Grand Silesia founded
diary.details: Crintera and Rethra sponsor Grand Silesia, the Order's easternmost covenant yet; its Bjornaer and the Bonisagi of Waldherz join the Rowan Gild.

diary.title: Tenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The Rhine's own gathering of this year is the first of three (997, 1004 and 1011) at which distrust within the Order stops the renewal of the Founders' vows at the Fane.

diary.title: Oakdell's charges dismissed (1136 AA)
diary.details: Oakdell's accusations of espionage and meddling against magi of Durenmar are thrown out as spurious and unproven.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1143 AA: the Rowan Gild Marched
diary.details: The whole Rowan Gild is Marched, beginning the Schism War in the Rhine. Severus Maximus of Flambeau declares Wizard's War on Caithlinn of Oakdell and Cirion of Tremere on Pietro of Oakdell; Tremere and Flambeau magi set about destroying Oakdell and Waldherz.

diary.title: New Slavonic Tribunal declared
diary.details: The Slavic covenants, Rethra and Grand Silesia among them, break with their sponsors and declare a New Slavonic Tribunal. Grand Silesia is destroyed the same year (the book's list of covenants says 1009).

diary.title: Oakdell razed (1155 AA)
diary.details: Oakdell is razed and all its Diedne magi slain in the Schism War.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1157 AA: the Schism War ends
diary.details: The Schism War is declared over; the Linden Gild grows up over the following decades. The renewal of the Founders' vows at the Fane resumes, an Ex Miscellanea magus taking the place Diedne's representative once held.

diary.title: Eleventh Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Over the Rhine's protests, the New Slavonic Tribunal is given authority over new covenants in Slavic lands.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1178 AA: Fengheld founded
diary.details: Veteran Tremere and Flambeau magi back from the Schism War in Britannia (fought in Stonehenge and Normandy) found Fengheld in the Harz with the Tribunal's ready approval, as a quiet retreat for ageing war heroes away from the mundanes.

diary.title: Fengheld's Tremere in Henry III's wars
diary.details: Through the reign of Henry III (1039 to 1056) Fengheld's political Tremere, working with the Transylvanian Tribunal, take part in the emperor's conquests of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary and seize many vis sites.

diary.title: Aschlaranda returns to Durenmar
diary.details: Aschlaranda, once of Waldherz, reappears at Durenmar.

diary.title: Dankmar founded
diary.details: Aschlaranda, exiled from Durenmar and from House Bonisagus, settles with her apprentice Schadrit at Dankmar in the Black Forest (the timeline puts their occupation of the site in 1053).

diary.title: Crintera allied with Pripet Maior
diary.details: Bjornaer magi once of Grand Silesia settle at Pripet Maior in the New Slavonic Tribunal, and Crintera and Pripet Maior form an alliance across the Tribunal border.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1192 AA: Guardians of the Forest
diary.details: The Guardians of the Forest ruling is made, allowing magi to defend wild places. Dankmar goes unrecognised as a covenant, Durenmar's influence seeing to it.

diary.title: Twelfth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: To curb the Rhine, the Grand Tribunal rejects its claim to the Polish lands left empty by Grand Silesia's fall and grants all Slavic lands to the New Slavonic Tribunal.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1206 AA: Roznov and Dankmar
diary.details: Roznov is founded in Moravia by three Ex Miscellanea magi, and Dankmar is at last recognised as a covenant of the Rhine.

diary.title: Roznov admitted
diary.details: Roznov is admitted to the Rhine Tribunal; two Tremere from Transylvania join it almost at once.

diary.title: Durenmar's charge against Dankmar
diary.details: Durenmar accuses Dankmar before the Tribunal of being secretly in league with the forest fay. Nothing is proven.

diary.title: King of the Black Mountain raids Durenmar
diary.details: The great faerie lord of the Black Forest attacks Durenmar; several Bonisagus magi and many covenfolk are killed or carried off, and the captives are never returned. In the years after, Durenmar's magi devise the most powerful Aegis of the Hearth yet known.

diary.title: First Treverorum proposal fails (1227 AA)
diary.details: Xantippes and Julia of Jerbiton and Selena Tibicena of Bonisagus propose a covenant in Trier to recover Roman secrets; with no sponsor from Irencillia, Crintera or Dankmar it is not recognised.

diary.title: Treverorum approved (1234 AA)
diary.details: The same three, now joined by Arliandus of Tremere, propose again and Treverorum is approved.

diary.title: Durenmar's lean half-century
diary.details: From about 1100 to 1150 Durenmar loses several magical sites to Zähringen settlement, runs short of vis and raids the forest's faerie sites greedily to make it up. The Black Fir begins to grow at the edge of its Aegis about this time.

diary.title: Valdus fined a pawn (1248 AA)
diary.details: Treverorum charges Valdus of Tytalus with twice harvesting vis from its site outside Trier's walls; he admits it but calls the site neglected and not theirs. The Tribunal rules that a site within a day's march of a covenant belongs to it, yet as Treverorum lost nothing Valdus pays one pawn and must ask leave in future.

diary.title: Rheinstein founded (1262 AA)
diary.details: Schwall of Bjornaer and Fulmonious of Tytalus found Rheinstein on Pfalz Island in the Rhine Gorge with the Tribunal's sponsorship, promising every other covenant a tithe of three pawns of vis a Tribunal for five Tribunals.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1283 AA: Oculus Septentrionalis founded
diary.details:
At the Ash Gild's urging the Tribunal resolves to learn more of the Norse wizards, the supposed Order of Odin, and orders a covenant founded for the purpose; three magi under Axior volunteer and Oculus Septentrionalis is born. The Tribunal rules that a covenant need have no site at its founding, only magi bound by a charter.

Secrets
Three Verditius magestones were secretly given to the new covenant.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1290 AA: Durenmar fined
diary.details: Dankmar accuses Durenmar of molesting faeries and plundering the Black Forest's faerie sites for vis. With Crintera, Irencillia and Fengheld, and the Hawthorn and Elder Gilds, behind the charge, Durenmar is fined a rook of vis to every other covenant and barred from faerie-site vis for fourteen years unless it makes peace with the fay; no such peace has ever been made.

diary.title: Triamore founded
diary.details: The newly risen Apple Gild founds Triamore at the court of Conrad III; Oculus Septentrionalis takes up the Gild as well.

diary.title: Redcap Ioanna murdered in Trier (1290 AA)
diary.details: The Redcap Ioanna is murdered in Trier; Treverorum denies all knowledge and a Quaesitorial investigation is ordered.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1297 AA: Oculus Septentrionalis fined
diary.details: The magi of Oculus Septentrionalis are found to have broken their charter: no site, no investigation, and still living in their old sancta. Each is fined three pawns of vis and ordered out of the old sancta within a year, with a permanent site to be found before the next Tribunal; two Jerbiton join them.

diary.title: Xantippes convicted of meddling (1297 AA)
diary.details: Xantippes of Jerbiton is found guilty of major mundane meddling, having worked Mentem magic of his own devising on the people of Trier for gain, to the harm of the Order's standing and perhaps a cause of Ioanna's death. He is fined ten pawns, his fortune is shared equally among the Tribunal's covenants and he owes three seasons' scribing to the Great Library.

diary.title: Agnes claims to have seen Merinita
diary.details: Agnes of Irencillia tells the Tribunal she has seen the Founder Merinita in Bohemia; few believe her.

diary.title: Hildegard of Bingen a Larta of Jerbiton
diary.details: Hildegard of Bingen is said to have been taken into House Jerbiton about this year as an unGifted maga under its protection and tutelage; she never attends a Tribunal and meets few magi, and the tale is unconfirmed.

diary.title: Oculus Septentrionalis settles in Lübeck
diary.details: About 1160 three magi of Oculus Septentrionalis settle in Henry the Lion's new city of Lübeck; Axior leaves them.

diary.title: Fifteenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: The Rhine again loses the Polish boundary dispute to Novgorod, as the New Slavonic Tribunal is now called.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1304 AA: the Lübeck charter
diary.details: Oculus Septentrionalis announces its new seat at Lübeck, and the Quaesitores force additions to its charter, among them that it admit only Gentle-Gifted magi.

diary.title: Treverorum fined fifty pawns (1304 AA)
diary.details: A Quaesitorial inquiry into the unrest in Trier finds Treverorum guilty of interfering with mundanes and the Church to the possible harm of its sodales; it is fined fifty pawns, payable by the next Tribunal, and ordered to repair its relations with the town.

diary.title: Terschelling founded
diary.details: Axior of Flambeau founds Terschelling on the Frisian island of that name. He dies in a magical accident within twenty years.

diary.title: Urgen Primus of Bjornaer
diary.details: Urgen takes the Primacy of House Bjornaer, which he holds through the Danish conquest of Rügen until 1203.

diary.title: Gathering of Twelve Years
diary.details: Jon Arnsson takes the Seat of the Stag on Crintera's council, a year before the Danes land on Rügen.

diary.title: Crintera enters Winter
diary.details: Valdemar I of Denmark conquers Rügen and Bishop Absolon breaks the temple of Arkona the next year. Over the Wilderists' objections Crintera chooses to wait the Danes out; the covenant falls into crisis and the Winter it has lived in for fifty years begins.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1311 AA: Treverorum abolished
diary.details: Scholastus of Jerbiton declares himself Treverorum's last survivor and the covenant is abolished; he calls Trier unsafe for magi because of its churchmen, gives no details and leaves for the Greater Alps. The fine is partly unpaid, so he is held liable and a Redcap request follows him. No one from Crintera attends.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1318 AA: Wizard's War on Prudentum
diary.details: Primus Urgen of Bjornaer charges Oculus Septentrionalis with aiding the Danish invasion of Rügen but offers no proof. Failing, he declares Wizard's War on its leader Prudentum of Jerbiton and kills him.

diary.title: Luctatio's crimes laid before the Tribunal
diary.details: Eule of Fengheld lays before the gathering her evidence that magi of Luctatio in the Roman Tribunal helped Milan beat Barbarossa at Legnano and that a necromancer of Vardian's Tomb made the plague that stopped his army before Rome.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1325 AA: Rügen and the Guardians ruling
diary.details: The Hawthorn Gild invokes the Guardians of the Forest ruling to strike back at the Danes on Rügen, with the Ash and, unexpectedly, the Elder Gilds in support. The Tribunal splits along factional lines and reaches no decision beyond a promised inquiry, so Crintera is refused leave to expel the Danes; several Bjornaer are prosecuted afterwards for attacking Danish settlers.

diary.title: Avarret Primus of Bonisagus
diary.details: Avarret becomes Primus of House Bonisagus and turns the House back to the conservative refinement of existing theory.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1333 AA: no wilderness invaded
diary.details: Held a year late because of the Grand Tribunal. Falke of Fengheld pleads passionately for Crintera to be allowed to resist the Danes, but Quaesitor Caecilius rules that no wilderness has been invaded or destroyed, Crintera's forest standing intact; the Guardians ruling is much narrowed and Crintera falls into factional infighting.

diary.title: Sixteenth Grand Tribunal
diary.details: Five magi of the Roman Tribunal are Marched over the Luctatio affair.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1339 AA: Rheinstein falls
diary.details: Horst of Mercere reports Rheinstein attacked and destroyed by an army of angry mundanes led by the archbishop of Trier, its magi's fate unknown; their own conduct drew the attention that undid them. The Tribunal bans all magical activity in the Rhine Gorge for twenty years.

diary.title: Terschelling turns to piracy
diary.details: Eric Ribecus and Hygwald Veritas join Terschelling and about this year kill a pirate chief and seize his three ships and their crews; the covenant takes to piracy, and Imanitos Mendax spends some years there as a guest soon after.

diary.title: Gathering of Twelve Years: Falke Prima
diary.details: Urgen resigns the Primacy of House Bjornaer but keeps the Seat of the Bear; Falke of Fengheld is elected Prima and takes the Seat of the Wolf.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1346 AA: Waddenzee
diary.details: Eric Ribecus and Hygwald Veritas announce they are the only magi left at Terschelling, rename it Waddenzee and change its charter and symbol. A Quaesitorial inquiry finds no wrongdoing, and a motion to treat it as a new covenant needing the Tribunal's leave narrowly fails, the Oak and Ash Gilds voting it down.

diary.title: Rethra abolished (1346 AA)
diary.details: The Tribunal declares the Slavic covenant of Rethra abolished, nothing having been heard from its magi for decades; the Knights of the Sword had lately desecrated and plundered its site (the book's list of covenants says 1202).

diary.title: St Georgen destroyed
diary.details: The monastery of St Georgen in the Black Forest is destroyed and its monks found dead among dark vines; Dankmar is suspected.

diary.title: God of Truth preached in Bohemia
diary.details: Over the last decade the religion of the God of Truth, preached by the prophet Iacob, spreads near the Bohemian Forest.

diary.title: Murion named Prima of Bonisagus
diary.details: Before his Final Twilight Primus Avarret names Murion his successor, passing over the better-qualified but 'too dangerous' Occultes and keeping the conservative line in charge of the House.

diary.title: Tribunal of 1214: St Georgen
diary.details: The latest Rhine gathering raises the destruction of St Georgen; Jiphella, Dankmar's only delegate, denies any part in it, and a close vote declines to investigate.

diary.title: Heorot founded on Zealand
diary.details: Three Rhine magi found Heorot on the Danish island of Zealand, on the site of Hrothgar's hall, in what is formally Novgorod's territory; Theoderich of Jerbiton leaves Oculus Septentrionalis to join them. It means to ask the Tribunal of 1221 for membership.

diary.title: The Gorge ban lapses
diary.details: The twenty-year ban on magic in the Rhine Gorge runs out. Durenmar's leadership, with no covenant founded for decades and Fengheld's chapters multiplying, sponsors newly Gauntleted magi to survey the Gorge's lost sites and found a new Middle Rhine covenant.

diary.title: Fengheld's Lusatia chapter and the border
diary.details: Fengheld, having been refused leave to sponsor daughter covenants of young Tremere, has lately founded a chapter house in Lusatia, ten miles from the agreed Novgorod border, provoking the latest boundary dispute between the two Tribunals; it has also loosened its Transylvanian ties, and Rudolph of Bonisagus proposes a Fengheld chapter at Durenmar itself.

diary.title: Fengheld's new masters and journeymen
diary.details: Imanitos Mendax attains Master rank at Fengheld, Beechleaf joins its main site, Felicia, Dorana's apprentice, passes her Gauntlet and Garrinchus is newly Gauntleted at the Rheingasse chapter.

diary.title: The Nebelkönigin stolen
diary.details: Waddenzee's pirates have lately taken the ship Nebelkönigin, with vis and books aboard, from Oculus Septentrionalis; as the Quaesitores had forbidden the trading venture she carried, the covenant cannot lawfully pursue her.

diary.title: Caprea blinds a peace envoy's familiar
diary.details: At Crintera the guest maga Caprea blinds the familiar of Carolus of Oculus Septentrionalis, sent as a peace envoy, and the two covenants' feud worsens.

gilds.name: Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The oldest and largest gild, a quarter of the Tribunal: tradition, respect for elders and the Founders, the Rhine's old glory. Led by Murion of Durenmar; Bonisagus, Guernicus and Tremere favour it.

gilds.name: Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The smallest: protects the wild places and beasts from mundanes and shuns contact with them. Led by Urgen of Crintera; mostly Wilderist Bjornaer.

gilds.name: Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Dominion over the land, a forthright Order, and (unspoken) war on the Order of Odin. Led by Philippus Niger of Durenmar; Flambeau, Tremere and Tytalus.

gilds.name: Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Split from the Hawthorn: the fae and friendship with them above all. Led by Iacob of Irencillia; nearly all of Irencillia and Dankmar, with a few Harmonist Bjornaer.

gilds.name: Linden Gild (Lindengilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. Founded after the Schism War by former Fengheld magi: co-operation, peace and an end to apathy; nearly a fifth of the Tribunal, the go-between. Led by Occultes of Durenmar; Mercere, Jerbiton, Verditius, Tremere and Trianoma's Bonisagus.

gilds.name: Apple Gild (Apfelgilde)
gilds.agenda: None: a member owes the gild their vote and reasonable aid. The newest and weakest: friendship with mundanes, acceptance, humility before God. Led by Henri de Tours of Oculus Septentrionalis, Wilhelm Weiss of Fengheld and Daria la Gris of Triamore.

tribunals.secrets: The Apple Gild, with Oculus Septentrionalis, Triamore, about half of Fengheld's magi and two covenants of Normandy, means to propose a new Lotharingian Tribunal over the Low Countries and the north-west at the Grand Tribunal of 1228; Waddenzee, though no friend of the Apple Gild, would join to escape the Rhine. The Ash Gild's older members quietly plan war on the Norse wizards beyond the Baltic, which Murion does not oppose. Eule of Fengheld, the likeliest Praeco by age, is in fact in Final Twilight, which her covenant conceals.

neighbours.name: The Black Forest
neighbours.summary:
The largest forest of western Europe fills the south-west of the Tribunal: over a hundred miles north to south and up to forty across, all hills under an unbroken canopy, with the Rhine plain to the west and the Neckar and the Swabian uplands to the east. Oak and beech grow on the lower slopes and fringes; in the centre and on the heights the fir stands so thick that no sunlight reaches the floor. There are no clearings, little level ground, a few villages at the edges and about a dozen monasteries drawn by the seclusion.

A Faerie aura of 3 lies over the whole forest, broken only by the Divine islands of its monasteries and a few Magic sites: Durenmar, the Fane of the Founders and the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls. Bears, boars and deer share it with stranger beasts; bockmen, goblins and giant bats hunt by night, villagers who go too deep vanish, and the few folk living inside are said to be half fay. Only the old Roman road crosses it; anywhere else is weeks on foot.

The forest was once the south-western part of the Hercynian Forest, cut off when the Romans built the limes, and its spirit split with it. The Cult of Mercury bound the greater part by its own oath-magic into what is now the Fane of the Founders, and the peaceful remnant withdrew to the Glade; a rebellious splinter fled south, dwindled, and regrew on mortal fear as the dark faerie King of the Black Mountain (Faerie, Might 60), who now rules every dark court of the forest. Since Durenmar's condemnation in 1151 the forest has been a hazard to magi, and no peace with the fay was ever made. The Swabian lands east of the forest, the Jura and the sources of the Danube, belong to this region too.

The Black Forest was the south-western part of the great Hercynian Forest until the Roman limes and the Black Forest Road of the first century cut it off; the Romans held its edges and never its heart. It became part of the duchy of Swabia, and from the eleventh century the Zähringen dukes cleared and settled its fringes, founding Freiburg in 1120, while Hirsau (1059) and its daughter houses such as St Georgen (1084) planted monasteries in its seclusion. The Hohenstaufen rose from their castle on the Kaiserberge nearby, and Barbarossa made Ulm a Free Imperial City in 1164. With the death of the last Zähringen duke in 1218 much of the forest's lordship passed to the Hohenstaufen; its interior remains unbroken wilderness, and the monasteries within it suffer attacks no one can explain.

neighbours.name: Dammërstein
neighbours.summary:
The Kohlergrund charcoal-burners call it the Stone House, and won't climb the spur after dark. A manor of grey granite sits on a spur above the Schattenbach valley, a day's walk south of the Black Forest Road through firs so close that only those who know the paths ever find it. Under its roofs the house runs back into the hill: stairs that go nowhere, galleries cut from the living rock, halls that open on more halls. A tall round tower rises at the edge of the bailey, its top storey ringed with windows. Below, carved into the cliff, a pillared front older than Rome stands around a door of polished black glass. On the ridge above, a Roman watchtower keeps its watch over nothing.

Magi founded it in the reign of the emperor Henry V and kept so much to themselves that the Rhine Tribunal half forgot them. Redcaps remember carrying letters there, then fewer, then none. Some say it was abandoned after a quarrel; some say it never existed.

details.tethers: The Founders' seven foundation stones, laid in a seven-circuit labyrinth under the manor's cellars

levels.name: The Echoing Halls
levels.see: Per + Awareness against 12, to notice the steps that lag
levels.enter: walk the spiral past the last cellar in darkness, counting the steps backwards; or Per + Enigmatic Wisdom against 12
levels.notes: High, dry halls where every footfall comes back a moment late, and sometimes before it is taken. Kyrillos's Hall of Echoing Steps is here, and Matthaios's sealed study opens off it.

levels.name: The Sealed Gallery
levels.see: a wall of black glass at the far end of the Halls, which reflects nothing
levels.enter: only for one who has seen through Seeming
levels.notes: No one has entered. Kyrillos sits before the wall for days.

tables.name: Exploring the house
tables.rows:
1: A roof has fallen in; rain and rooks in a Founder's hall.
2: A store-room of broken lab-ware, every vessel labelled in Greek.
3: A corridor that comes back to where it began, though it never turned.
4: An apprentice's cell, with a child's drawing of the tower scratched on the wall.
5: A stair down to a cellar that isn't on any plan Gertrud knows.
6: A Founder's door, sealed with wax and a sigil no one has broken.
7: A gallery cut through to the cliff, with a view down the whole valley.
8: Footsteps ahead, which stop when you stop.
9: A cache: a few pawns of old vis, or a book thought lost.
10: A stair that wasn't there yesterday, going down.

tables.name: A night in the Halls
tables.rows:
botch: Your own footsteps lead you away; you wake in another part of the house.
1-3: Nothing but the echoes, a moment late.
4-5: Echoes that come before the steps.
6-7: Kyrillos's voice from an empty room, finishing a sentence.
8-9: A breath of warm air from the far end, where the black wall is.
10+: For an instant the black wall shows a reflection, and it isn't yours.

tables.name: What the valley says of the Stone House
tables.rows:
1: The magi all died in one night, and the barefoot monk buried them under the hill. (SG: False: only Kyrillos knows their fates.)
2: The monk in the cellars is the last of the old magi, and he hasn't eaten in nine years. (SG: Half true: he's a Founder, and he eats.)
3: There's a stair in the manor that's only there some nights. (SG: True: the Echoing Halls.)
4: The old Duke gave the magi the whole valley, from the narrows to the springs. (SG: True: the Founders' charter.)
5: The baron wants the spur, and only what's still up there keeps him off it. (SG: True.)
6: A woman of the house made a bargain with the forest folk and never came back. (SG: True: Hildegund.)
7: Lights have been seen in the round tower again. (SG: True.)
8: The black door in the cliff is older than Rome, and it opens onto Hell. (SG: Half true: older than Rome; not Hell.)
9: Gertrud's family stayed because they're paid in silver that never runs out. (SG: False: they stayed out of loyalty.)
10: Lutz says the magi left a room full of vis they never used. (SG: True: the Founders' sealed quarters.)

tables.name: What the Tribunal says of Dammërstein
tables.rows:
1: Nobody is sure Dammërstein still stands; the Tribunal half forgot it years ago. (SG: True.)
2: A Redcap tells of Vim silk sold at a Tribunal fair, spun somewhere in the Black Forest. (SG: True: the Whispering Well.)
3: Letters in the archive at Durenmar speak of a spell that held more vis than its Art allows. (SG: True: the Deeper Vessel.)
4: A scrap of an older faith names a place "where the glass drinks the gods' gifts". (SG: True: the Obsidian Crucible.)
5: A Bonisagus there built a laboratory of black glass that drinks vis. (SG: True.)
6: Coeris sent a Tremere there, and still wants to know what she learned. (SG: True: Ilona.)
7: The Founders fell out over who would claim a breakthrough. (SG: Half true: that was one of three causes.)
8: The Criamon there went into Twilight long ago and never came out. (SG: False: Kyrillos is still there.)
9: The Founders were hiding something from the Quaesitores. (SG: Half true: from each other, mostly.)
10: A magus of Dankmar visited once, and won't say why. (SG: True: Orphedra.)

tables.name: Behind a sealed door
tables.rows:
1: Dust, a cold hearth, and a chair pushed back as if someone had just stood up.
2: A room that is larger inside than the wall outside allows. (SG: The house's regio, leaking.)
3: Shelves of empty vis jars, each labelled in a different Founder's hand.
4: A nest of martens in the bedding, and a Founder's ring among the straw.
5: A stair going down that wasn't on any plan. (SG: The Echoing Halls.)
6: A wax seal stamped with five marks, unbroken, on a second door behind the first.
7: Kyrillos, sitting in the dark, who says he was waiting for you.
8: A wall of Greek written in charcoal, Matthaios's sums, broken off mid-line.
9: Cobweb so thick across the far door that it hums. (SG: The Spinner's thread reaches here.)
10: A room exactly as it was on the last night of 1211: supper on the table, five places laid, one plate untouched.

tables.name: Down the Echoing Halls
tables.rows:
botch: The way back isn't there. The halls go on, and the echoes have stopped answering.
1-3: Steps, and their echoes a moment late.
4-5: A door in the rock that opens on a room you left an hour ago.
6-7: Barefoot prints in the dust, going both ways at once.
8-9: A gallery of carved faces older than Rome, all turned toward the same wall.
10-11: Kyrillos at the end of the hall, walking away from you without moving.
12+: The black wall of the lowest gallery, and writing in it that wasn't there before. (SG: The stone Kyrillos read in 1201.)

tables.name: At the gate this season
tables.rows:
1: Bread left by the burners, and a child who runs when the gate opens.
2: Lutz and his sons with the stores, and news from the Kinzig valley.
3: Konni Matthissohn with the rent, wanting to know who to pay now.
4: A Redcap, footsore, with letters and a question about the lights.
5: One of the baron's serjants, counting chimneys from the road.
6: Mother Agathe, who walks in without knocking, as she did for the Founders.
7: A pedlar of Strassburg glass, who has heard the house buys panes. (SG: Matthaios's panes are running out.)
8: A hedge-witch from the next valley, asking for shelter and an apprentice's place for her daughter.
9: Small grey folk on the wall at dusk, wanting a story for passage through the Hollow.
10: A magus of the Tribunal, uninvited, curious about what the Founders left.

tables.name: Trouble in the household
tables.rows:
1: Gertrud and the new cook at war over the kitchen.
2: A grog who heard footsteps on a stair that isn't there, and won't stand his watch.
3: Food going missing from the stores, and barefoot prints in the flour. (SG: Kyrillos eats after all.)
4: Sigismund has found a book in the library that he says reads itself aloud at night.
5: A Kohlergrund girl courting one of the household, and her father up at the gate about it.
6: Someone has broken a wax seal on a Founder's door, and nobody will say who.

neighbours.secrets:
Four ages lie on top of one another here. The cave behind the cliff façade was a sanctuary of the god the Romans called Mercury, set beside Abnoba, the forest's lady; the Romans raised the watchtower on the ridge; the Founders built the manor in 1115 and, over ninety years, each added to it until it ran right through the hill; and since 1211 it has been a ruin, where the oldest work stood up best.

The Founders came for different reasons. What brought Matthaios was a Cult of Mercury fragment that named "the place where the glass drinks the gods' gifts". What brought Kyrillos is sealed beneath the hill, behind the Sealed Gallery: what it is, and what it does to magic, is the saga's to decide.

The façade in the cliff is Celtic, older than Rome's coming; the Romans called its god Mercury. Its altar was a slab of Theran obsidian, now the heart of the Athanor (the Obsidian Crucible's card).

neighbours.name: The Obsidian Crucible
neighbours.summary:
Behind the black door in the cliff lies the old shrine cave. To most eyes it is a dry store-room of barrels and broken lab-ware. But the walls are not rock. Every surface, floor, walls and the low dome of the roof, is laid with black volcanic glass, fitted so close that no blade could find a seam. Matthaios of Bonisagus brought the glass in carts from Thera, a sea and an empire away, and spent twenty years setting it.

Touch the door with a pawn of Vim and it opens on another room, the same shape but larger. The glass there is warm, and the air hums like a struck bell.

details.tethers: The obsidian door, set in the shrine's ancient façade

levels.name: The Crucible
levels.see: Per + Magic Lore against 9, to feel the warmth in the glass
levels.enter: touch the obsidian door with a pawn of Vim vis, which isn't spent
levels.notes: The laboratory is here. The glass drinks light and holds heat, and spent vis leaves faint glowing veins in it. There is no deeper level.

tables.name: The glass is listening
tables.rows:
1-2: The glass is cold and dull, as if it were only stone.
3-4: The hum rises half a tone when the vis is opened.
5-6: Veins of light run through the walls towards the Athanor.
7-8: Your reflection in the dome moves a moment after you do.
9: A word in Greek, in Matthaios's voice, from somewhere in the glass.
10: The whole chamber rings, and every vessel on the shelves sings with it.

tables.name: Working in the black glass
tables.rows:
botch: The glass drinks something it shouldn't, and the laboratory is very cold for a day. Someone smells hot iron where there's none.
1-3: The dome hums faintly, and the work goes as it should.
4-5: Your reflection in the glass finishes a movement a moment after you do.
6-7: The vis in the vessel seems to settle, as if something were holding it.
8: A Greek word, spoken from the glass, correcting your method. (SG: The Voice in the Glass.)
9: Warmth where there should be none, and the smell of the sea near Thebes.
10-11: For a moment the whole dome shows a different laboratory, older, with a man working in it.
12+: The glass rings like a struck bell, and every pane in the house answers it.

tables.name: What the Voice wants
tables.rows:
1: Vis, and nothing else. It falls silent until a pawn of Vim is opened.
2: To be told the year, and who leads House Bonisagus now.
3: That his notes be read aloud to him, from the sealed study.
4: To know who else has worked in his laboratory, and what they did with it. (SG: He is jealous of the Crucible.)
5: A promise that the Deeper Vessel will be read out at Durenmar under his name.
6: Nothing. It is listening, and that is worse.

diary.text: The god the Romans call Mercury is honoured in the cave behind the cliff, and his altar of black glass drinks the gifts laid on it.
Matthaios finds the altar stone in the cave and knows it for Theran obsidian.
Matthaios sets the last of the Theran glass in the Crucible: floor, walls and dome, twenty years after the first cart came up the valley.
Matthaios builds the Athanor around the altar slab.
The great skein's silk is brought to the Crucible, for the Deeper Vessel.
Theodoric writes from Durenmar that he has seen a spell hold more than its Art allows. Matthaios works through the winter.
Matthaios's last night: he opens all his Vim on the altar slab at the heart of the Athanor and makes himself the Vessel, and the glass takes him.
A young magus of Bonisagus comes up the valley to work in the black glass.

links.note: Who lined it with Theran glass
Matthaios on the shrine and its cult

neighbours.secrets:
The shrine. The cave behind the cliff was the sanctuary of a Celtic god whom the Romans called Mercury, as Caesar says the Gauls' chief god was: the pillared façade is Celtic and older than Rome's coming, the dedication Roman. Its cult kept a Mystery here, "the place where the glass drinks the gods' gifts", which is what brought Matthaios.

The altar stone. The glass the fragment meant was the shrine's altar: a single slab of black volcanic glass that drank the offerings laid on it, which the cult said came from an island of fire in the east. In 1115 Matthaios knew it for Theran obsidian, from the island Plato's Atlantis is drowned beside, and in Mythic Europe the glass of a volcano that swallowed a civilisation is magic. So he spent twenty years bringing more from Thera to line the whole cave, and made the cave into the altar. The slab is the heart of the Athanor, the oldest glass here, and an ancient magical artefact: a source of insight for Original Research (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages). Theran glass holds vis without decay.

The Deeper Vessel. The Crucible is Matthaios's instrument for it, the Major Breakthrough he sought: a new Hermetic Virtue letting spells take in more vis than the usual limit. He reached about 30 of the 45 breakthrough points it needs.

Matthaios is in the glass. On the last night of 1211 he opened all his Vim on the altar slab in the Athanor and made himself the Vessel, and the glass took him the way it takes vis. He is a Magic spirit here now: The Voice in the Glass, on the Bestiary. Rows 7-8 and 9 of the table are him. He holds the insight for the last 15 breakthrough points, and a magus who works here, speaks Greek and keeps him in vis can have it, one experiment a season. Whoever takes over this laboratory is moving into a dead man's instrument with the dead man still in it.

The laboratory. Everything in it was built for experiment and for getting the most out of vis, which makes it less suited to anything else (its Lesser Focus). The glassware is Venetian, bought through a Venetian factor by way of Matthaios's letters to Durenmar: he had the craft to set obsidian, not to blow fine glass. The Rowan Lectern keeps the Spinner's lesser folk, Might 15 or less, from whoever reads at it; it does not keep out the Spinner.

Taking over the laboratory (Take over the laboratory, on its Planning tab): its Refinement is 2 and it already has Predecessor, so the storyguide's secret roll can add no second one. If it is made a magus's laboratory while the covenant is In Creation, it may be treated as that magus's starting laboratory and the season skipped.

neighbours.name: The Abnoba Watchtower
neighbours.summary:
A Roman signal tower of dressed stone on the ridge above the manor, from the days when the frontier ran through these hills. Latin letters to Abnoba, the forest's lady, cover its inner walls, and each winter they weep a clear resin. The Founders took stone from its walls for the manor; most of it still stands.

Shepherds say a legionary still keeps watch on the ridge at night, and that something old and coiled sleeps in the water under the floor. Their dogs won't go near it.

details.tethers: Abnoba's altar, in the lowest room

triggers.name: The inscriptions weep
triggers.what: The resin can be gathered: 2 pawns of Intellego, after the first drop is burned as Abnoba's due. Left ungathered, it drips into the pool in the flooded strongroom.

triggers.name: Abnoba's due
triggers.what: At the solstice: was the first drop burned on the altar with the watchword? If so, the serpent's track does not move this winter. If not, and its pool has reached its Might (20 pawns, from Winter 1220), move the Serpent Under the Watchtower one place along its track.

diary.text: The Eighth Legion raises the tower on the ridge as it builds the road, and plants Abnoba's grove below.
The serpent comes up out of the springs for the resin. The century burns Abnoba's due, and it sleeps.
The frontier falls and the century is ordered out. Gaius Vettius, the signifer, stays with the pay-chest to wait for an officer.
No one burns the due. The serpent wakes and kills the signifer at the altar, then drinks and sleeps.
The five gather the Abnoba Watchtower's weeping resin for the first time. The signifer on the ridge salutes them.
The last winter the five gather the resin.
The resin goes ungathered, and drips through the floor into the flooded cellar.
Nine winters' resin in the pool now: 18 pawns. The water under the floor is warmer than it should be.
The pool reaches 20 pawns. At the solstice, either the due is burned, or the serpent stirs.

tables.name: A night on the ridge
tables.rows:
botch: The water under the floor is warm against your boots, and something long turns over beneath it. It knows you were here.
1-2: Wind through the empty windows, and nothing else.
3: Sheep tracks lead up to the doorway, and none lead away.
4: The lettered walls are wet to the touch, out of season.
5: A shepherd's dog howls on the slope below and won't come any closer.
6: Someone has burned resin on the altar not long ago. It wasn't you.
7: A wolf-skin cloak, grey as ash, hangs on a nail by the altar. In the morning it's gone.
8: A legionary stands at the eastern wall, looking toward a frontier that isn't there. He doesn't turn.
9: A challenge in Latin out of the dark: the watchword, or leave.
10-11: The legionary salutes you, as if you were someone he once knew, and points down at the floor.
12+: Lamplight through a gap in the flagstones shows black water, the bronze corner of a chest, and a coil as thick as a man's waist.

tables.name: What the shepherds say
tables.rows:
1: A legionary keeps watch on the ridge on winter nights. (SG: True: the signifer.)
2: Something coiled sleeps in the water under the floor. (SG: True: the serpent.)
3: The letters on the walls curse whoever reads them. (SG: False: they honour Abnoba.)
4: Sheep that drink near the tower in hard winters are found dead without a mark. (SG: True.)
5: The Romans buried their gold under the tower. (SG: Half true: silver, the pay-chest.)
6: The magi went up every midwinter with a lamp and came down singing. (SG: Half true: they burned Abnoba's due.)
7: The ghost will speak to you if you know the soldiers' word. (SG: True: "Abnoba vigilat".)
8: The walls weep because the forest's lady mourns her soldiers. (SG: A folk tale: the resin is vis.)
9: A baron's man went up for a dare and didn't come down. (SG: False.)
10: The tower and the old firs below were raised together. (SG: True: the Hochtannen.)

tables.name: Burning Abnoba's due
tables.rows:
botch: The watchword comes out wrong, and the water under the floor goes still, the way a hound goes still.
