neighbours.name: Kohlergrund
neighbours.summary: A dozen households of charcoal-burners and herders in the valley under the spur, where the smoke from the clamps hangs in the firs. For as long as anyone remembers they have paid a small rent in coin and charcoal to the Stone House, and in return no wolf, sickness or tax-man troubled them much. The rent went on being paid after the lights went out. Now someone has lit them again. The burners leave bread at the gate and wait to see what kind of master has come.

tables.name: On the Schattenbach
tables.rows:
1: Charcoal-burners with a loaded cart, who touch their caps and won't meet your eye.
2: Mother Agathe with her basket, who knows your business before you say it.
3: A herd-boy looking for a strayed goat near the Mirror Tarn.
4: Lutz and his sons on the road with the stores, glad of company.
5: The baron's toll-men at the chain, wanting a bridge-penny where there is no bridge.
6: Loggers from the camp, drunk and looking for trouble.
7: A raft of fir trunks going down, its raftsmen singing.
8: A factor of Rudolf Kalb's, measuring trees and asking about the ruin.
9: Grey silk across the path, and humming somewhere close.
10: Wolfram himself, with four riders, who wants to know who you are.

tables.name: Talk at the clamps
tables.rows:
1: Pay the gate or pay the baron, but nobody can pay both much longer. (SG: True. They'll stop paying whichever master looks weaker.)
2: The wolves came back the year the flood took the stone at the river. (SG: True: the wards failed in 1213.)
3: The new masters up the hill are wizards, and wizards eat bread left at the gate. (SG: Half true: the old servants took it in.)
4: The coin left at the gate these eight years is still up there somewhere. (SG: True: about two pounds of pennies, in the gatehouse.)
5: Konni will pay whoever keeps the baron's men off the clamps. (SG: True.)
6: Old Grete has a box under her bed worth more than the whole valley. (SG: True, though nobody knows why.)
7: Bärbel looked into the tarn too long; ask her if you want the truth about it. (SG: True.)
8: The abbey at Gengenbach wants the forest penny stopped as much as we do. (SG: True.)
9: Father Hugo doesn't know half of what old Father Anselm knew. (SG: True: Anselm sealed Liese's secret.)
10: The baron's going to burn the hamlet if the wizards don't knuckle under. (SG: False, so far.)

tables.name: What the hamlet needs this season
tables.rows:
1: Wolves at the folds again, and the herders want the old circle drawn.
2: A sick child that Mother Agathe can't reach in time.
3: The forest penny due, and not enough coin for it and the gate's rent.
4: A clamp that won't draw, and the burners say something is sitting on it at night.
5: Konni wants to know, plainly, whose side the Stone House is on.
6: The Gengenbach priest is coming up, and somebody needs a marriage, a burial and a blessing all at once.

diary.text: Ilona of the Stone House draws a circle round the hamlet, a furrow set with stones, and no wolf crosses it.
A burner's wife comes home from the high firs with a child that isn't her husband's. They call her Liese.
Liese bears Jörg's daughter, Grete, the spring after he went down, and makes the fiddler's song.
Agathe, twelve years old, follows the lady from the Stone House into the forest, and is not sent home.
Agathe goes down to the Whispering Well for Hildegund and comes back with the sight, and with something she can't say.
Liese dies. The priest writes down what she tells him and seals it in a box for Grete.
The lady from the Stone House draws the circle for the last time.
Hildegund passes Agathe's door for the last time, and asks her to keep leaving the milk.
The spring flood takes the stone sill where the circle crosses the Schattenbach. No one comes down from the Stone House to mend it.
The baron's men come up the valley for a forest penny. No one has ever asked one before.
Wolves in the valley again, the first in living memory. Rupert loses three ewes.
Agathe keeps the baron's little Gertrud alive.
Lights in the Stone House. The burners leave bread at the gate, and the rent beside it, and wait.

links.note: The wise woman at the head of the valley
Who went down into the webs in 1162

neighbours.secrets:
The wards. The protection was Ilona's: two Ring wards on one circle drawn round the hamlet, a furrow set with stones, crossing the Schattenbach on a stone sill. Circle Against the Grey Hunter kept out wolves; Ward Against the Pestilent Air kept out the foul airs that carry pestilence (her own spells, on her card). She drew the circle anew every seven years from 1122 to 1206, for the Contest of the Gate. In the spring of 1213 the flood took the sill, and there was no warden to mend it. That winter the wolves came back. The valley has noticed without knowing why.

The tax-man was never kept out by magic: no ward of Ilona's would break the Code. The Founders' charter covered the land above the narrows, and the Schattenbachs never came up. Wolfram's men came in 1213 because the lights had gone out and the wolves were back.

Paying twice. Since 1213 the baron's men have taken a forest penny from every hearth, and the burners still leave the old rent at the Stone House gate. Paying twice is breaking them, and they pay a tithe to Gengenbach besides. Before the winter of 1220 is out they will stop paying one of their masters, and it will be the one who looks weaker. The covenant's Contested Resource Hook on their rents is this: unless the Stone House stands up for them, the rent stops.

Is the forest penny lawful? Partly. The burners' clamps eat timber, and the timber of the whole valley is Wolfram's by his grandfather's grant, so he may rightly charge for the wood they cut. But he takes it as a penny from every hearth, the herders' too, at a rate he set himself, without asking the Founders, who hold the ground. That is why Duke Berthold V let it pass in 1213, and why the Schultheiss at Offenburg would split it: a fair wood-fee from the burners, nothing from the herders. The covenant can secure the rents without a fight by settling a wood-fee with him, or paying it for the burners; under the Contested Resource rule that secures them for five years.

Who speaks for it. Konni Matthissohn, Grete's son, about 35, is the clamp-master: he brings the rent up to the gate, and the burners' word is his. He is Liese's grandson, so he has the King Fir's blood and doesn't know it: the rent, the box under Grete's bed and the King's line are all in one house. He is careful, slow to speak, and owes nobody; he will pay whichever master can keep the baron's men off the clamps.

The Church. Kohlergrund has no church. It belongs to a Kinzig valley parish served from Gengenbach Abbey, and the priest comes up at Easter and Michaelmas to baptise, marry and bless the graves. Father Anselm, who took down Liese's secret in 1190 and sealed it for Grete, is dead. Father Hugo, the priest now, is young and doesn't know the box exists. Gengenbach takes its tithe, and has every reason to want the baron's penny stopped: it is a quiet third party.

The rent at the gate. From 1212 to 1220 the rent was left at the gate and Kyrillos's handful of old servants took it in. The charcoal went into the hearths; the coin, about two pounds of pennies, is in a chest in the gatehouse, the covenant's to find.

Its people: a dozen households, about seventy souls, burners at the clamps on the slopes and herders on the valley floor. Grete Liesestochter is the oldest woman down in the hamlet; Mother Agathe, three years older, lives apart at the head of the valley.

Bärbel, a herder's widow of thirty-eight, is the girl who looked into the Mirror Tarn too long. In the summer of 1198, at sixteen, she came home with the face of a woman of forty, and no one knew her. Now at last she looks her age: her face has been waiting for her. She is the one person in the valley who will tell the covenant plainly what the tarn does.

neighbours.name: Rudolf Kalb of Strassburg
neighbours.summary: A cloth-and-timber merchant of Strassburg, soft-spoken and well fed, who has never set foot in the Black Forest and never will. He lends to knights who have trees. He has heard of firs in the Schattenbach valley taller than any in the Empire.

details.wants: The Hochtannen firs, as great beams for the cathedral works at Strassburg, which has been rebuilding since the fire of 1176
details.offers: Money, lent at interest; the clearing of a knight's debts

tables.name: Word from Strassburg
tables.rows:
1: A letter to the baron, carried by a carter who reads it first and tells the whole valley.
2: Kalb's factor at the narrows, counting trees and asking about the ruin on the spur.
3: A raised offer: the debts cleared, and something over, for the eldest firs.
4: A reminder, politely worded, that Martinmas 1222 is nearer than the baron thinks.
5: An approach to the covenant: Kalb would sell the baron's paper to anyone who paid him for it. (SG: True. He doesn't care who.)
6: News that the cathedral works at Strassburg want beams by next summer, and will pay anyone who brings them.

tables.name: Dealing with Kalb
tables.rows:
1: He answers within the month, politely, offering to sell the baron's paper.
2: His factor wants to see the money before he'll name a price.
3: He asks, delicately, whether the gentlemen on the spur also have trees.
4: He has heard of the covenant from someone in Strassburg, and is curious who.
5: He'll sell, but only if the cathedral still gets its beams from somewhere.
6: He's already sold part of the debt on, to a cousin in Basel. (SG: Storyguide's choice whether it's true.)

neighbours.secrets:
He holds all of Wolfram's debts. He never comes himself; he sends letters and, once a year, a factor.

Christians may not lend at interest, so Kalb writes no loans: he buys. Each sum Wolfram took was written as the price of the Schattenbach forest's yield for some years ahead, with the forest rights themselves pledged as surety. The account comes to about ninety pounds of Strassburg pennies, far more than two poor manors can raise. Unless it is paid by Martinmas 1222, the forest rights pass to Kalb in pledge, and his men will fell the whole valley, the Hochtannen first. His offer to clear it all for the Hochtannen beams stands until then. He would sell the debt to anyone who paid him for it, and he doesn't care who.

neighbours.name: The Spinner's Court
neighbours.summary:
Go down into the Hollow, past the grey sails of web that hang between the leaning firs and the warmth that has no business being there in winter, and at the bottom of the silk you will find a woman at a wheel. She is the loveliest thing you will ever see. Afterwards you won't be able to say whether her hair was dark or fair, or her eyes kind or cruel. You'll only remember that you wanted her to keep looking at you. Her voice is low and fond and faintly amused, as if you had already said something foolish and she had already forgiven you. Behind her, on the webs, her shadow works with too many arms, and it doesn't stop when her hands do.

Whatever is whispered to her she spins into thread, fine as breath and grey as ash, and the thread goes up into the dark. She will trade for anything you could want. She'll name a price, and the price is always a secret.

details.rules:
Her word is iron. Every bargain she strikes binds her as tightly as it binds you, and she will keep it to the letter even when it bleeds her. She is careful with her words for exactly that reason.

Daylight cuts thread. Tell a secret openly, under the sun, to three listeners, and its strand in her web snaps. It is the only blade that can hurt her web, and it cuts both ways: a secret spoken that freely is spent for its teller too.

A secret must be given. She can't steal one, wring it out, or read it from a sleeping mind. It has to be breathed into her ear, or down the well. So she doesn't take. She tempts.

Guest-right. Whoever eats or drinks at her wheel is safe from her and all her court until the next dawn. Whoever comes uninvited and refuses her cup has no such shelter, and Old Spindleshanks knows the difference.

Her name is the one thread she cannot spin. Nobody at court knows it, perhaps not even Hush; the valley sang it once, and has forgotten. A mortal who learned it would hold the only debt she could never repay.

Never thank her. A thank-you acknowledges a gift, and a gift acknowledged at her wheel is a bargain struck with the price left blank, which she may name whenever she likes. You don't thank her; you pay her. The cup is the one exception: drinking from it accepts guest-right, which has its own terms.
details.wants: Secrets, and the King of the Black Mountain on his knees
details.offers: Vim silk, favours, passage, and older things, always for a secret

tables.name: What she asks
tables.rows:
botch: Your name. Not a secret about you, but the thing itself. Refuse and she laughs, and asks again next time.
1-2: A small shame: something you did and never told.
3-4: Someone else's secret, one that wasn't yours to give.
5-6: A secret of the covenant: a password, a flaw in a ward, where a vis store is kept.
7-8: A secret about someone you love, that would hurt them if it were spoken.
9: A secret of the King's, or of something he reaches for. If you haven't one, she will wait while you fetch it.
10+: The secret you would least want spun. She knows which one it is.

tables.name: Gossip at court
tables.rows:
1: Haspel: the King's hunt rides at the new moon. (SG: True.)
2: Haspel: the King fears the Fane of the Founders. (SG: True, and no use to anyone.)
3: Jörg: Liese's hair was fair and her laugh was like a jay's. He has been here a season, maybe two.
4: Hush: "Who sits on the second stool, and why is her thread never finished?"
5: One of the small grey folk: the Stone House's pact cost more than a secret a year. (SG: True. Mother Agathe knows.)
6: Haspel: the Spinner was once a mortal woman. (SG: False: Haspel is testing you.)
7: Jörg: there is a tune that stops the wheel. He has forgotten it.
8: Hush: "What did the woman from the valley carry down, forty years ago?"
9: A courtier offers a secret about a magus of the covenant, in trade for one of yours.
10: Someone says the Spinner's name by accident, and the court goes silent; no one will repeat it. Int + Faerie Lore against 12 recalls a Kohlergrund song with that one syllable in it.

tables.name: A night at court
tables.rows:
1: Dancing, and Dame Haspel won't let anyone sit down.
2: Jörg plays, and the tune is one the valley stopped singing sixty years ago.
3: Hush moves among the guests asking questions, and every answer costs something.
4: A courtier offers a secret about the King of the Black Mountain, for one about the Stone House.
5: The Spinner asks a guest to sit beside her at the wheel, on the first stool. (SG: The second stool is Hildegund's.)
6: A woman on the second stool spins without looking up, and hums a Founders' song. (SG: Hildegund.)
7: Haspel tells, laughing, of the King's last hunt, and who it rode down.
8: The feast is wonderful, and in the morning it was moss and well water, but no one is hungry for a day.
9: Old Spindleshanks shifts in the dark above, and the whole court falls silent until it settles.
10: Dawn comes, guest-right ends, and the Spinner smiles at whoever is still there.

reasons.what: The silk pact lapsed as the Founders drifted apart: about twenty years of skeins with no secret paid. To her the debt is the Stone House's, whoever lives there now.
New faces at the Stone House, and so a new story, which she finds delicious.

favours.what: Hildegund's first favour, worth 80 Build Points (Hidden Resources): vis, a faerie-worked effect, books or a season of labour, for the Spinner's price
Hildegund's second favour, worth 80 Build Points, on the same terms
Hildegund's third favour, worth 90 Build Points, which only Hildegund can call in
The silk pact's arrears: a whispered secret for each skein the Well spun since the pact lapsed, about eighty

neighbours.secrets:
She owes the King of the Black Mountain nothing, and she means to see him kneel.

Her web is woven of secrets, and its strength runs backwards from what mortals expect. A secret everyone knows is gossip, worth nothing. A secret held by two is a cord. A secret held by one, and then whispered to her, is a cable she can climb, and each strand binds her to whatever the secret touches: a man, a lineage, a mountain, a crown. To unthrone the King she must hold his secrets, and also the secrets of everything he reaches for: his vassals, his treasures, the lords who pay him tribute without knowing it, the Hollows and hills he means to have next. It's patient work. She is ageless, almost no one knows she exists, and she hasn't made an enemy yet. She doesn't hunt. The well does that for her, singing up through the Black Forest to anyone clever and hungry enough to come.

One account is still open, and it has never left the Hollow. In the autumn of 1211 Hildegund of Merinita came down into the webs to pay the pact's forfeit, and she is there still. She sits on the second stool beside the wheel, half guest and half thread, and doesn't count the seasons. The Spinner keeps her for the one thing no faerie can make for itself: a creative mortal who can reshape a faerie's role. With Hildegund's hands in her glamour and enough encased well silk to feed the change, she means to become something the King must kneel to (the hoard is on her Bestiary card, and its clock on the Hollow's Triggers). Of the three favours Hildegund bargained on the way down, the first two were struck in full. The third sits on her books like a dropped stitch: Hildegund sat down at the wheel before its price was named, so only she can finish it. The Spinner would rather keep her than settle either the third favour or the arrears. She doesn't know the silver spindle exists.

At the table: faerie, ruler of the Spinner's Court (the Faerie Court Hook), with a Faerie aura of 5 throughout the Hollow. She can go anywhere she pleases, and seldom wants to. Her stat block is on her Bestiary card. The old pact cost the covenant one whispered secret a year for each skein of well silk. It lapsed as the Founders drifted apart. Renewing it now costs a secret that costs the teller something: one that would hurt or shame them, or another's that wasn't theirs to give. Each renewal is a scene. By the precedent of 1180, one great secret may secure five years of skeins at once, the five years for which the app secures a Contested Resource.

When the pact lapsed in 1200 the forfeit fell due. In the autumn of 1211, after the others had gone their ways, Hildegund walked into the Hollow to pay it. She was the one who loved it best. On the way down she bargained three favours for the house in return for going willingly. She is the surety for the arrears: about eighty secrets, one for each skein spun since 1200. When they are paid, or bargained down and paid, the forfeit ends and she may walk out, and the Spinner cannot stop her: her own first law and the Binding Oath both hold her to it. The Spinner would much rather the arrears stayed unpaid, because Hildegund is worth more to her than eighty secrets, so she will haggle, delay and never volunteer the terms.

She is the story. Long before the Founders, before the Romans, the Hollow belonged to something vast in the webs that took strays and wrapped them away: Old Spindleshanks. The valley feared it, and the fear had a name; mothers used it to keep children from the Hollow, and burners said it to curse a broken cart. Over the centuries the valley told itself a softer tale to live beside it: a woman at the bottom of the webs, at a wheel, who would let you pass if you whispered her your secret and paid her price. Faeries are made from such stories (Realms of Power: Faerie), and the story stood up and sat down at the wheel. Her shadow is its shadow: that is why it works with too many arms and does not stop when her hands do. Spindleshanks serves her because she is the face it wears for mortals and the bargain it offers them; without her it would be a hungry thing in the dark again, and the valley would stop telling stories about it, which a faerie fears more than iron. Neither remembers. Spindleshanks is not cognizant enough to, and the Spinner never knew: she believes she is the mistress and it her hound.

Her true name is the horror's old name. That is why it is the one thread she cannot spin: it isn't a secret, it is what she is made of. It is one syllable, and it survives in one place, the last verse of the fiddler's song. After Jörg went down, Liese made the song, and as a King's daughter who knew what names are for she put the old name in its last verse, meaning to sing it at the Wheel and fetch him back. She never dared, and on her deathbed she made Grete promise the verse would never be sung. Spoken to her, the name works her Sovereign Ward: she cannot harm whoever knows it, and its touch destroys her body. The name is Wurt: Old High German for fate, kin to the English wyrd and to Urðr, the Norn who spins it. To the valley's oldest tongue the horror in the webs was simply Fate, the thing that takes you whatever you do; the softer story made it a woman who spins your fate for a price. No one in Swabia uses the word now.

Destroy the Spinner with her name and the story ends, but the horror does not. The Hollow goes back to being a larder: no bargains, no guest-right, no woman at the wheel, only Spindleshanks in the dark and hungry. Kohlergrund pays first.

The pact of 1115 was a plain bargain: four skeins of well silk a year, each for one whispered secret. In 1180 the Founders wanted more, because Matthaios needed vis for the Deeper Vessel. For one great skein, paid for once with a single great secret, the Spinner asked that the pact be sworn again under Binding Oath, with its forfeit. The forfeit's words had to be whispered by someone outside the house, so Hildegund sent Agathe down the Well with them. The great skein set the precedent: one great secret may stand for several years of skeins.

neighbours.name: The Serpent Under the Watchtower
neighbours.summary: Something long sleeps in the flooded cellars beneath the Abnoba Watchtower. In hard winters sheep are found at the water's edge with no mark on them, only very still.

stages.title: It stirs
stages.clues: The water under the floor is warm. Dogs howl at the ridge.
stages.ignored: It drinks the pool, and wakes enough to dream.
stages.stopped: Abnoba's due is burned at the solstice, or the resin is gathered and the pool drained: it sleeps another year.

stages.title: It dreams
stages.clues: Those who sleep near the tower dream of coils, and wake knowing things they shouldn't, true things.
stages.stopped: Abnoba's due is burned, and the resin gathered: it sinks back into sleep.

stages.title: It wakes
stages.clues: Sheep gone from the folds. A track like a dragged log across the snow.
stages.ignored: It hunts the ridge by night, cleverer than any beast, and it has learned to speak.
stages.stopped: It is driven back below, or slain.

tables.name: Signs under the ridge
tables.rows:
botch: Whoever slept nearest the tower last night wakes knowing a stranger's secret, and the serpent knows theirs. (SG: The Dreams of the Coil, whatever its stage.)
1-3: Nothing. The ridge is cold and the water is still.
4-5: The water under the floor is warmer than the air above it.
6: Dogs howl at the ridge all night.
7: A ewe at the water's edge, dead without a mark, only very still.
8: A shepherd boy who dreamed of coils and woke knowing where a lost knife was. (SG: From the second stage.)
9: The signifer on the ridge, staring down at the floor, not east.
10-11: A track like a dragged log across the snow, from the tower to the folds. (SG: Only once it wakes.)
12+: Something in the strongroom speaks, in a voice like water, and asks who keeps the watch now. (SG: Only once it wakes.)

tables.name: Dreams of the Coil
tables.rows:
1: The taste of resin, and nothing more.
2: Where something lost was hidden, and it's true.
3: A Latin word, over and over: the watchword. (SG: "Abnoba vigilat".)
4: The face of someone in Kohlergrund, and a thing they've never told.
5: The weight of coins pressing on their chest all night.
6: The serpent's own thought, cold and patient: that it has waited long enough.

neighbours.secrets:
A magical serpent, mostly dormant: something to be aware of rather than a constant threat. Its stat block is on its Bestiary card.

It came for the Intellego resin the inscriptions weep. Gathered each winter as Abnoba's due, the resin keeps it asleep; the Founders stopped around 1211. Since then the resin has dripped through the floor and pooled in the flooded cellar: 2 pawns a winter, 18 by Spring 1220. In Winter 1220 the pool reaches its Might, 20, and it drinks. Each later stage comes only if that winter's resin also goes ungathered. Gathering the resin and draining the pool starves it; the pool itself is 18 pawns of Intellego vis, if someone dares take it from around a sleeping serpent.

Its hoard is the legionaries' pay-chest. The signifer on the ridge remembers how the Romans kept it asleep.

How it moves. It is a track, not a calendar: it moves one place each winter that Abnoba's due goes unburned once its pool has reached its Might (20 pawns, from Winter 1220). A winter with the due burned does not move it. The Watchtower's trigger "Abnoba's due" asks the question each solstice. The years on the stages are when each would come if nobody did anything.

Abnoba's due. The first drop of each winter's weeping, burned on the altar at the solstice with the watchword spoken ("Abnoba vigilat", the lady keeps watch), is her due; the rest is the covenant's 2 pawns. The rite is what the serpent answers to: gathering the resin keeps it hungry, and burning the due keeps it asleep. The Founders kept the rite from 1115 to 1210, which is why the signifer saluted them.

neighbours.name: Grete Liesestochter
neighbours.summary: The oldest woman down in the hamlet of Kohlergrund is Grete, whom everyone calls Liese's Grete, because she never had a father to be named for. She keeps bees, sets bones, and keeps a small iron-bound box under her bed that she won't open and won't sell. When children sing the fiddler's song, she makes them stop before the last verse.

details.wants: To be left her box; for the children to stop before the last verse; her family kept safe
details.offers: Honey, bone-setting, and the oldest memories in the valley

tables.name: What Grete tells you
tables.rows:
1: That her mother Liese married the fiddler, and he went down into the Hollow the winter before she was born. (SG: True.)
2: That the bees go quiet whenever the King's hunt rides at the new moon.
3: That the old wards round Kohlergrund were a lady's, and the flood took the stone at the river. (SG: True: Ilona's wards, the sill in 1213.)
4: That the children mustn't sing the last verse, and she doesn't know why. (SG: True. It holds the Spinner's name.)
5: That her granddaughter Liesl sees the little grey folk, and she wishes she didn't.
6: Nothing about the box. She changes the subject, kindly and at once.

tables.name: A visit to Grete's house
tables.rows:
1: The bees are restless and she sends you away until they settle.
2: A bone to set, a burner's boy, and she wants a magus to hold him still.
3: Liesl at the door, saying the little grey folk came again last night.
4: Grete, ill, wanting someone to promise to keep the box safe. (SG: Liese's secret.)
5: A Kohlergrund child singing the fiddler's song in the lane, and Grete out of the house to stop her before the last verse.
6: A stranger asked about the box yesterday. (SG: Someone of the Spinner's, or Haspel's.)

neighbours.secrets:
Jörg and Liese's daughter, born in the spring of 1163, the spring after he went down; she is 57. The box holds Liese's secret, written down by the parish priest at her deathbed in 1190 and sealed. Grete has never read it.

The secret Jörg has waited sixty years for is still in the world, and Grete holds it. If it went to the Spinner it would make a thick strand. If it went to Jörg, he might finally ask to leave.

Liese was the King Fir's daughter. About 1140 a burner's wife of Kohlergrund came home from the high firs with a child that wasn't her husband's. Liese grew up fair, quick and a little uncanny, married Jörg the Fiddler, and never told him: that was the one thing she always held back.

Her family: her husband Matthis the burner is dead. Her son Konni works the clamps; her daughter Elsbeth is married to Rupert the herder; she has five grandchildren. So the King's blood runs, thin, through a third of Kohlergrund, and none of them know. The youngest grandchild, Liesl, has the old uncanniness and sees the small grey folk (Faerie Blood, as does Grete; the rest have nothing).

What the box is worth: to the Spinner, a cable straight into the King's lineage, and the means to pay Jörg at last; to the King, a line he never knew he had; to Jörg, the answer and the end of waiting; to the covenant, a terribly valuable thing in a burner's widow's house, with Haspel watching who goes down to the Wheel.

She stops the children before the last verse of the fiddler's song because Liese made her promise to on her deathbed. She doesn't know why. The verse holds the Spinner's true name.

If Jörg ever walks out, the first person he meets is his daughter: thirty years older than he looks, and a stranger to him.

neighbours.name: The Founders of Dammërstein
neighbours.summary: The five magi who built the Stone House on the spur above the Schattenbach in 1115: Matthaios of Bonisagus, Kyrillos of Criamon, Nikephoros of Tytalus, Ilona of Tremere and Hildegund of Merinita. They came north from the Theban Tribunal and Coeris, swore an accord to share what they found, and kept to themselves so well that the Rhine Tribunal half forgot them. Their trust broke around 1200, and after a last quarrel in 1211 four of them were gone within a year. Only Kyrillos remains. Its Diary has what the house remembers of them.

details.rules:
The accord, in Ilona's hand, sworn in 1115; the whole of it is Dammërstein's Charter. Her commentary, The Covenant Accord, gives it clause by clause; the clauses scored through she struck out herself, each in the year it failed. The five the Founders wrote first:

What the house finds. What any of the five finds here, under the hill, in the Crucible or in the forest, is shared with all five. (Scored through, 1201: Kyrillos, and the stone in the lowest gallery.)

The council and the warden. The house decides in council, each Founder one voice. The warden keeps the accord and the keys of the sealed quarters, and calls the council.

Nothing beyond the house. Nothing of the house goes to the Tribunal, to any House or to any covenant without the consent of all five. (Scored through, 1205: Matthaios's thirty years of letters to Durenmar. She never scored it for herself, though Coeris asked her for thirty years.)

The Spinner's people. The house deals with the Spinner's people through Hildegund alone, and the pact's secrets are paid by the house, each Founder giving in turn. (Scored through, 1200: no one paid.)

A Founder who leaves. A Founder who leaves takes only what is theirs, and their quarters are sealed until the council opens them. This is why the Founders' quarters are sealed still.
details.wants: Each came for their own reason: Matthaios for the Deeper Vessel, Kyrillos for what lies sealed under the hill, Hildegund for the Spinner's court, Nikephoros for the contest, and Ilona because Coeris sent her.
details.offers: Nothing now: the five are scattered. What they left is the house's: the 1115 charter, their books and sealed quarters, the Crucible, the silk pact and its arrears, and Hildegund's three favours.

diary.text: The five come north and take the spur above the Schattenbach, by Duke Berthold III of Zähringen's charter, drawn up through a Strassburg notary in Nikephoros's pay.
Hildegund goes down into the Spinner's Hollow and makes the Stone House's peace with the Spinner's people.
The first skein of the silk pact at the Whispering Well: four pawns of Vim, each paid for with a whispered secret.
The five gather the Abnoba Watchtower's weeping resin for the first time. The signifer on the ridge salutes them.
Ilona raises her first wards over the valley, and Nikephoros breaks them before the year is out. She raises them again, stronger. The Contest of the Gate begins.
Matthaios sets the last of the Theran glass in the Crucible: floor, walls and dome, twenty years after the first cart came up the valley.
A Tytalus of Thebes declares Wizard's War on Nikephoros. Ilona holds the house's wards against him for a season.
Matthaios's first letter to Theodoric of Bonisagus at Durenmar, about how much vis a spell can hold. He tells no one at the house.
The great skein: the five swear the silk pact again under Binding Oath, with its forfeit, for Matthaios's extra silk. Agathe of the valley carries the forfeit's words down the Well.
The last skeins paid for under the pact.
No one comes down from the Stone House to the Hollow, that year or the next. The silk is left on the webs, and the oath marks each of the five.
Theodoric dies at Durenmar. Matthaios's last letter to him comes back unanswered.
Ilona finds Matthaios's thirty years of letters to Durenmar and scores the accord's clause Nothing beyond the house through.
Ilona renews the valley's wards for the last time, and Nikephoros tests them for the last time.
The last winter the five gather the resin.
The last quarrel. Hildegund walks into the Hollow and does not come out. Matthaios is not seen after this year.
Nikephoros leaves.
Matthaios's last night: he opens all his Vim on the altar slab at the heart of the Athanor and makes himself the Vessel, and the glass takes him.
Ilona leaves. The household drifts away, and for a decade no light shows on the spur. Kyrillos stays.
At Coeris, Nikephoros fights Benedek of Tremere in certamen for Ilona, who cannot cross the threshold uninvited, and loses.
Nikephoros gives up on a rematch and goes south, to the Alps.

tables.name: What the house remembers
tables.rows:
1: A cup left on a table in 1211, still with a ring of wine in it.
2: Ilona's hand in a margin of the Accord, striking a clause through, and a year beside it.
3: A Greek word scratched into a pane of glass: Matthaios's. (SG: He casts no reflection in it.)
4: Nikephoros's chessboard, mid-game, with a piece missing.
5: Wool and a spindle left on a windowsill, and a hum from somewhere you can't place. (SG: Hildegund, at the Wheel.)
6: A threshold scored with Tremere marks, as if someone wanted to be asked in. (SG: Ilona's Flaw.)
7: A door sealed with five seals, one of them broken. (SG: A Founder's quarters.)
8: Kyrillos in a doorway, saying that's not the way, and closing it.
9: Letters in Latin to Durenmar, never sent, about a vessel deeper than its Art. (SG: The Deeper Vessel.)
10: All five names cut together into a lintel, with the year 1115, and one name cut deeper than the others.

tables.name: In the Founders' quarters
tables.rows:
1: Nikephoros's: a certamen ring scorched into the floor, and a ledger of every contest he won.
2: Nikephoros's: a mirror turned to the wall. (SG: The Mirror of Contest.)
3: Ilona's: Tremere seals on every letter, and a threshold she scored with her own knife.
4: Ilona's: letters from Coeris, each asking the same question in a different way.
5: Hildegund's: a spinning wheel with no thread, and wool gone grey on the floor.
6: Hildegund's: a song written out in her hand, with the last verse scraped from the page.
7: Matthaios's: no mirror anywhere, and the window glass taken out.
8: Matthaios's: thirty years of letters from Durenmar, tied in bundles by year.
9: A shared room: the Accord on the table, its clauses scored through one by one.
10: A store of mixed vis, labelled in Nikephoros's hand: "for the next contest". (SG: His cache.)

links.note: Who found the place, and built the Obsidian Crucible
The last of the five, still in the deep halls
The warden, who wrote the accord
Who made the peace with the Spinner's people

neighbours.secrets:
Why it fell. Three things broke them, together: jealousy (of Matthaios's Crucible and the claim House Bonisagus might make on its results, and of what Kyrillos kept to himself), pressure from Coeris on Ilona, and ninety years without a result. Trust broke around 1200; after that the vis went unharvested, the pacts lapsed and the household drifted away, until a last quarrel in 1211. (Also in the covenant's secrets.)

How the accord was broken. Kyrillos broke the first rule around 1200, when he read the stone in the lowest gallery and told no one. Matthaios broke the third for thirty years, writing to a sodalis at Durenmar about the Crucible. Ilona was pressed to break it by Coeris and never did. The fifth is why the Founders' quarters are still sealed.

The oath and its marks. The five swore the silk pact under Binding Oath in 1180. When they let it lapse in 1200, each took a Flaw from it and hid it from the others. Kyrillos cannot refuse a whispered question (Lesser Malediction). Nikephoros: every lie he tells is heard as a lie (Greater Malediction). Ilona cannot cross a threshold, in or out, unless she is invited. Matthaios casts no reflection in glass or water. Hildegund heard the Wheel every night (Compulsion), until she went down to pay the forfeit.

The five fates, as Kyrillos believes them, and as they are. Matthaios: Kyrillos read in the Crucible's glass that he went into the regio in 1211 and met Final Twilight; but Matthaios casts no reflection, and the glass's memory of that night has a gap the shape of a man, which Kyrillos filled with what he expected. Matthaios is in the glass: on the last night of 1211 he made himself the Vessel, and the Crucible took him the way it takes vis. He is a Magic spirit there now, The Voice in the Glass, on the Bestiary. Nikephoros: Kyrillos is sure he is alive in the south, and he is: at the threshold of the Cave of Twisting Shadows since 1217, after losing a certamen to Benedek of Tremere at Coeris in 1212. Ilona: Kyrillos thinks she is alive and silent at Coeris; she is alive, but outside it, in the village under the castle, because Benedek will not invite her in. Hildegund: Kyrillos hears her humming in the webs, and she is at the Wheel as the pact's forfeit. Kyrillos: still under the hill, waiting for younger magi to guard his body while he looks for the Axis Magica.

The Founders' fates are known only to Kyrillos, and he has his own agenda. Each Founder's character card has the whole of their story.

tables.name: Rumours of the Stone House
tables.rows:
1: There are letters in the archive from a Bonisagus of the Black Forest, thirty years of them, on Vim. (SG: True: Matthaios's, a few stray ones.)
2: Theodoric's correspondent claimed a spell could hold more vis than its Art allows. (SG: True: the Deeper Vessel.)
3: Ricardus Caespuus has a fir under glass that came from the Black Forest, and won't say where. (SG: True: the Hochtannen cutting.)
4: Dammërstein was dissolved years ago, and its seat is anyone's. (SG: False, as far as anyone at Tribunal has ever ruled.)
5: The Founders came from Thebes with a ship's hold of black glass. (SG: Half true: Theran glass that Matthaios brought from near Thebes.)
6: A Criamon is still there, and he hasn't been seen at Tribunal in thirty years. (SG: True: Kyrillos.)
7: The Tremere there was sent by Coeris to spy on the rest. (SG: Half true: Coeris pressed her, and she never told.)
8: Lights have been seen on the spur above the Schattenbach this year. (SG: True.)
9: House Bonisagus has a claim on whatever was found there. (SG: Half true: the claim House Bonisagus might make on the Crucible's results.)
10: A Merinita of the Stone House went to the faeries and never came back. (SG: True: Hildegund.)

tables.name: On the road to the Schattenbach
tables.rows:
1: Raftsmen walking home up the Kinzig, cheerful and broke.
2: A Redcap, who asks whether you're bound for the Stone House, and what you've heard.
3: Pilgrims for Strassburg, who ask for a blessing.
4: A carter missing a wheel, cursing the baron of Schattenbach.
5: A Gengenbach monk with the tithe-rolls, wary of strangers.
6: Wolves at dusk, closer than they should be this far down.
7: Kalb's factor on a good mule, with a measuring rod across his saddle.
8: A peddler selling grey silk that hums when you hold it. (SG: Stolen from the Well, or a fake.)
9: Roman paving under the mud, and a milestone with the legion's number on it.
10: A rider in the baron's colours, who turns back toward the narrows the moment he sees you.

characters.name: Kyrillos of Criamon

background.birth_name: Kyrillos, son of Ioannes the ropemaker
background.title_profession: Magus of House Criamon, Founder of Dammërstein

description.physical_description: Tall, spare and barefoot; looks sixty; a close white beard; Criamon stigmata cover his scalp and hands; his shadow lags a pace behind.
description.biography:
Born in 1090 in Thessalonica, the son of a ropemaker, Kyrillos was found at ten by a Criamon of the Clutch of Xylinites, who heard him describe the quarrel that had cracked an old jar in his father's shop, a quarrel fifty years past. He passed his Gauntlet in 1105 and spent ten years in the Theban Tribunal as a reader of objects and a witness the Tribunal called on when it wanted to know what really happened. He went on returning to Thebes for its Tribunals for a century, and the four apprentices he trained at Dammërstein all went home to the House in the East.

In 1115 he came north with Matthaios of Bonisagus, who had found something in a Cult of Mercury text, and with Nikephoros of Tytalus, Ilona of Tremere and Hildegund of Merinita, who chose the site for its faerie neighbours. Each came for reasons of their own. Kyrillos came for what lies sealed beneath the hill. They swore an accord to share what they found, and kept to themselves so well that the Rhine Tribunal half forgot them. Over the decades their trust wore thin; by about 1200 it had broken, and the work they did together dwindled to nothing: the vis went unharvested, the pacts with the faeries lapsed, the household drifted away. After a last quarrel in 1211 the other four were gone within a year. Kyrillos remains, with a handful of old servants, among the ruins.

He has walked the Path of Seeming for a century, through four Stations: Differentiation of Seeming (which gave him Clear Thinker, Common Sense and Keen Vision), True Sight (his Enigmatic Wisdom serves as Second Sight and Magic Sensitivity; the Vow came from it), Vivid Memories from Objects (the Flashbacks are its Ordeal), and Passing Through Seeming (the Visions are its Ordeal). The fifth, the Station from Which to Ignore the Real, can only be reached at the Axis Magica on New Year's Eve, and he has not tried it.

Vow: never to destroy an object whose memories he has not first read.

Longevity: he made his own ritual in 1130 and renewed it in 1209, after an Aging Crisis broke the old one (Aging modifier -8).

Twilight scars (Warping 7): his shadow walks a pace behind him and turns at corners he did not take; his skin is marked with faint blue labyrinths that rearrange themselves while he sleeps; he hears an object's last spoken word when he first touches it; candles lean towards him in still air.

Appearance: a tall, spare Greek who looks sixty, with a close white beard, a shaved head covered in Criamon stigmata, and very pale grey eyes that rarely blink. He wears undyed linen, walks barefoot indoors, and speaks Latin with a Constantinople accent and High German slowly and carefully.

Talisman: the Labyrinth Mirror, a palm-sized polished bronze disc with a seven-circuit labyrinth cut into its back and a rock crystal at the centre. Laboratory: the Hall of Echoing Steps, a labyrinth of passages cut into the rock beneath the ruins of Dammërstein and opening into its regio.

hermetic.wizards_sigil: His spells leave the faint echo of footsteps in a stone corridor.

characters.summary:
A tall, spare Greek who looks sixty and is far older: a Criamon of the Path of Seeming, trained at the Clutch of Xylinites in Constantinople, who still speaks Latin with a Constantinople accent. The Theban Tribunal remembers him as the witness it called when it wanted to know what really happened; in the Rhine almost no one remembers him at all.

He lives in the deep halls under the Stone House in the Black Forest, the last of the five who built it. Visitors hear his footsteps in the passages before he arrives. He answers questions with questions, and he reads the history of every stone and post he touches.
characters.secrets:
Everyone at Dammërstein had their transgressions; his was the one that set the rest alight. Around 1200 he read the memory of a stone in the lowest gallery and saw the first piece of the secret: where the way in lies, and that it opens only for one who has seen through Seeming. He told no one. When the others learned he had kept it, the jealousy already there (over Matthaios's Crucible and the claim House Bonisagus might make on it), the pressure Ilona was under from Coeris, and ninety years without a result did the rest.

He knows, or believes he knows, what became of each of the four, and tells no one unless it serves him. Matthaios: he read in the Crucible's glass that Matthaios went into the regio one last night in 1211 and did not come out the same way; he thinks it was Final Twilight. He is wrong: the glass's memory of that night has a gap the shape of a man, where it could not see Matthaios, and Kyrillos filled it with what he expected. Matthaios is in the glass (The Voice in the Glass, on the Bestiary). Nikephoros: alive, he is sure, and still contesting the secret somewhere in the south. Ilona: alive at Coeris and silent, which worries him more than any threat. Hildegund: he watched her go down into the Hollow in the autumn of 1211, and she never came out. On still nights since, he has heard her humming down there, a murmur from deeper in the webs than the Hollow ought to go. He has never gone after her, and he has never told anyone she is alive.

He believes the last part of the way in needs the Station from Which to Ignore the Real, and that Dammërstein's regio may lead to the Axis Magica. He needs younger magi to guard his body while his spirit travels, and he will recruit them without telling them why.

The silk pact was a Binding Oath, and Kyrillos let it lapse with the others. Around 1200 he was warned by a memory of grey thread, and took no notice. Since then he has carried a faerie Flaw he has never explained: he cannot refuse a question asked of him in a whisper, though he may answer as obliquely as he likes. The other Founders were marked too, each in their own way.

He swore the Binding Oath of 1180 with the others, so he knows the forfeit to the word, and he knows that paying the arrears, or bargaining them down, would free Hildegund. He has not paid them. The secrets would have to be his own, and the Spinner always comes at last to the secret you would least want spun. For him that is the way in under the hill. He fears giving her that more than he loves Hildegund, and he knows it. His love for her is philia and pragma, not eros: the friendship of equals who chose the same road, and the patient, practical love of a century of keeping one house together, since she came north at twenty-one and laughed at his questions. It is not a lover's. And it was his silence about the stone that broke the house, let the pact lapse and sent her down. He carries that too.

His mark is on his sheet as Lesser Malediction, outside the Virtue balance. Nikephoros found it out. In the last quarrel of 1211 he whispered his question, and Kyrillos had to answer: the last part of the way in needs the Station from Which to Ignore the Real, which is reached only at the Axis Magica. Kyrillos knows Nikephoros knows, and that is why he is sure his old friend is somewhere in the south.

One of The Founders of Dammërstein: the faction card, under The Region, Factions, has the five's accord, Diary, marks and fates together.

His "Go, then" in the spring of 1212 was the invitation that let Ilona out of the house. He doesn't know her mark, so he doesn't know that.

The Mirror Tarn. Reflections there look startled or annoyed to be seen; one that meets the eye calmly belongs to something that isn't what it seems. For a century he has gone down to the water to test a thing, and he still does. He knows how to lift the reflections at the equinox.

characters.name: Matthaios of Bonisagus

description.physical_description: A tall, stooped Greek who looked seventy, with a white beard kept short against the furnace, burn scars on both forearms, and veins of faint light on the backs of his hands where spent vis ran.
description.biography:
Born in 1080 in Thebes, a glassblower's son. A Bonisagus of the Theban Tribunal found him at nine, reckoning his father's furnace temperatures by the colour of the glass, and he passed his Gauntlet in 1097. He was the oldest of the five. In a Cult of Mercury fragment he read of "the place where the glass drinks the gods' gifts", and in 1115 he brought the others north to find it.

He found it in the shrine cave behind the cliff, and spent twenty years lining it with obsidian he brought in carts from Thera, a sea and an empire away, until the last of it was set in 1135. In it he built the Athanor and the Obsidian Crucible, and spent his life testing how much vis a spell can hold. He wrote On the Bounds of Power (a Vim summa), The Measure of the Art, The Pawn and the Spell, Of Fire That Does Not Consume, The Gate of Mercury and others, and copied The Lamp of Durenmar.

From 1173 he wrote to Theodoric of Bonisagus at Durenmar, against the accord's clause Nothing beyond the house, for thirty years. In 1180 the great skein was sworn for his extra silk. When the pact lapsed in 1200 the oath marked him: he casts no reflection (Lesser Malediction, outside the Virtue balance). Theodoric died in 1203, and in 1205 Ilona found the letters and scored the clause through.

On the last night of 1211, after the last quarrel, he made himself the Vessel, and the Crucible's glass took him. He is there still, as The Voice in the Glass (on the Bestiary). This card keeps him as he was that night.

Virtues and Flaws: Puissant Magic Theory is House Bonisagus's Virtue. Driven is the Deeper Vessel. Difficult Spontaneous Magic: he never trusted magic made up on the spot.

Longevity: his own ritual of 1125, renewed in 1170 and 1200 (Aging modifier -9). He looked seventy by the end.

Twilight scars (Warping 6): the glass warms when he is near; spent vis leaves veins of light on his hands.

characters.summary: A theorist of vis from Thebes, ambitious and exacting, who read of this place in an old Cult of Mercury text and brought the others here. He built the Obsidian Crucible and spent his life in it testing how much vis a spell can hold. For thirty years he wrote to a sodalis at Durenmar about it. He has not been seen since 1211.
characters.secrets:
The truth. He is in the Crucible's glass. On the last night of 1211, after the last quarrel, he opened all the Vim he had left in the Athanor and cast it into his own body, to be the Vessel himself. The Theran glass drinks whatever vis is opened in it. A reflection is the one thing that stays outside the glass, and since 1200 he had none, so the glass drank him too. He is a Magic spirit there now: The Voice in the Glass, on the Bestiary. This card keeps him as he was in 1211.

He sought the Deeper Vessel, a Major Breakthrough: the new Hermetic Virtue it would give lets a spell take in more vis than the usual limit. He reached about 30 of its 45 breakthrough points. His sealed study in the Echoing Halls holds his journal, the insight Lab Texts of his two stabilized Discoveries, and his revised On the Bounds of Power (Level 16, Quality 12), which he never let out of the study; the library has the first version. The spirit holds the insight for the last 15 points.

His mark. Each Founder took a Flaw from the Binding Oath for letting the pact lapse in 1200, and each hid it from the others. His: he casts no reflection in glass or water (Lesser Malediction, outside the Virtue balance). He hid it even from Kyrillos. Kyrillos read the glass's memory of that night and found a gap the shape of a man, where the glass could not see Matthaios, and filled it with what he expected: Final Twilight.

One of The Founders of Dammërstein: the faction card, under The Region, Factions, has the five's accord, Diary, marks and fates together.

characters.name: Nikephoros of Tytalus

description.physical_description: A compact, handsome Greek who looks fifty-five, with black hair gone iron at the temples, a duellist's quick hands and a smile he uses like a blade. He dresses well for the road and talks to everyone.
description.biography:
Born in 1087 at Larissa in Thessaly, the son of a horse-dealer who could sell a lame mare twice. A Tytalus of Thebes found him at twelve, arguing a bishop's steward out of a tithe, and he passed his Gauntlet in 1104. In ten years in the Theban Tribunal he fought more certamina than any magus his age. He met Kyrillos of Criamon across a Tribunal floor, and they were friends and opponents from that day.

In 1115 he came north with the others for the pleasure of the struggle. He was the covenant's diplomat and duellist. Through a Strassburg notary in his pay he got Duke Berthold III's charter for the spur and the valley. He wrote Of Minds and Their Doors (a Mentem summa), The Breaking of Wards and The Spear Through the Shield, and in 1150 he made the Mirror of Contest.

In 1180 he swore the Binding Oath with the others. When the pact lapsed in 1200 it marked him: every lie he tells is heard as a lie (Greater Malediction, outside the Virtue balance). It took his best weapon. In the last quarrel of 1211 he whispered his question to Kyrillos and got the answer: the Axis Magica. He left that winter.

In 1212 he lost a certamen to Benedek of Tremere at Coeris, fighting for Ilona, which made Benedek and Coeris his enemies (Enemies). In 1216 he bought maps of the Alps in Venice. Since 1217 he has been at the threshold of the Cave of Twisting Shadows, trying to win his way to the Axis Magica by contest.

Virtues and Flaws: Self-Confident is House Tytalus's Virtue. The Gentle Gift is why the Founders sent him to the Duke. Driven is the secret under the hill.

Longevity: his own ritual of 1135, renewed in 1200 and again in 1212 after the certamen (Aging modifier -7). He looks fifty-five.

Twilight scars (Warping 5): his voice carries a faint second voice under it, a half-beat behind, that says what he means; his reflection salutes before he does.

Enchanted device: the Mirror of Contest (on this card), left in the sealed Founders' quarters.

characters.summary: A Greek of Thessaly, Kyrillos's oldest friend and opponent, who came for the pleasure of the struggle. Clever, charming and quarrelsome, the covenant's diplomat and duellist. He left in the winter of 1211.
characters.secrets:
The truth. He is alive. He left in the winter of 1211, and in the summer of 1212 rode to Coeris and challenged Benedek of Tremere to certamen for hounding Ilona. He lost, badly. He cannot lie about it, so he has never told it, and the Tribunal decided he must be dead.

In 1211 he had whispered his question to Kyrillos, and learned the answer: the last part of the way in needs the Station from Which to Ignore the Real, reached only at the Axis Magica. That is the regio of the Cave of Twisting Shadows, House Criamon's home in the Alps (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). In 1216 he was in Venice buying maps, and by 1217 he was at the Cave.

He is there still, in 1220. He means to win the way through by contest. The Criamon will not contest him; they answer with enigmas. And he can no longer bluff, because every lie he tells is heard as one. It is the only contest he has ever lost by being honest. He is a rival for the same door Kyrillos wants, and he could come north for allies, or for his Mirror.

Ilona and Nikephoros: pragma, not a romance. It is no young lovers' affair but the deep, abiding love of ninety-seven years of knowing, testing and respecting each other, of truly knowing someone and valuing what you find. He is a Greek and a Tytalus, and he honours someone by testing them with everything he has; she is the one person at Dammërstein who never once lost to him and never once gloated. Neither has ever said it. Both, now, long to be together again. (Ilona's card has the whole of it: Aristophanes' halves, the Contest of the Gate, their marks, the debt of 1158, Coeris, and now.)

"Never left the Black Forest" is only valley talk.

Each Founder took a Flaw from the Binding Oath for letting the pact lapse in 1200, and each hid it from the others. His: every lie he tells is heard as a lie, a Major Flaw for a Tytalus diplomat. He can no longer win by guile, only by open contest, which is why he left looking for someone to contest the secret with.

What the Order says (rumours, none confirmed): a Redcap says he was seen in Venice in 1216, buying maps of the Alps; a Tytalus at the last Tribunal swore he died in a certamen in Hungary; others say he never left the Black Forest at all. He thought the secret could be won by contest, and was looking for someone to contest it with.

One of The Founders of Dammërstein: the faction card, under The Region, Factions, has the five's accord, Diary, marks and fates together.

Aristophanes' halves. In Plato's Symposium, Aristophanes tells how the first people were cut in two, and each half goes through life looking for the other. Nikephoros, a Greek, knew the speech by heart; the Latin West barely knows the book. The last leaf of The Breaking of Wards ends with one line of it in Greek, untranslated, the only line in the book that isn't a joke. Ilona learned Greek in the 1180s, telling the others it was to check his citations. Her unsent letters from outside Coeris end with the same line, in her careful Greek. Neither has ever seen the other's.

Coeris, 1212. He knew her mark, so when he heard she had gone home he knew Benedek would leave her outside the gate. He rode straight there, found her standing in the road, and wagered for exactly what she needed: Benedek's invitation in, or his promise to leave her be. He lost, in front of her, the first contest she ever watched him lose, and he could not lie about it afterwards. invented_spells.name: Circle Against the Grey Hunter
invented_spells.description: The caster inscribes a circle that no wolf will cross. It is Circle of Beast Warding narrowed to one kind of beast, so the herders' sheep and dogs come and go. A Circle may be any size the caster can draw, and a Ring spell lasts until the line is broken. Ilona drew hers round Kohlergrund as a furrow set with stones. (Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Ring)

invented_spells.name: Ward Against the Pestilent Air
invented_spells.description: Turns back at the circle the foul and corrupted airs that physicians blame for pestilence, as Ward Against the Sirocco turns back breezes carrying dust. While it stands no pestilence carried on the air reaches those within; ordinary illness, and sickness from food, water or touch, still does. No Hermetic ward stops a disease itself. (Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Ring)

description.physical_description: A tall, straight woman who looks sixty, with iron-grey hair in a single plait, a Magyar's high cheekbones and a level stare. She dresses plainly and well, and she stops at every doorway.
description.biography:
Born in 1092 near Esztergom, a castellan's daughter. Benedek of Tremere took her to Coeris at nine, and she passed her Gauntlet there in 1110. Coeris sent her north with the others in 1115 to learn what Matthaios had found, and she became the house's warden and wrote its accord.

For ninety-seven years she kept the house's wards, its accord and its keys. Every seven years from 1122 she renewed the wards over the valley, and every time Nikephoros tried to break them (the Contest of the Gate). In 1158 she held the house against a Wizard's War declared on him. She wrote The Rule of the Hand (a Rego summa), The Iron Hand, Against Hasty Experiment (at Matthaios) and The Covenant Accord, whose clauses she scored through as they failed.

Benedek pressed her for decades, in letters still in her sealed quarters, to send Coeris what Dammërstein hid. She never did. When the pact lapsed in 1200 the oath marked her: she cannot cross a threshold, in or out, unless she is invited (Greater Malediction, outside the Virtue balance).

In the spring of 1212 Kyrillos's "Go, then" let her out of the house. Benedek would not let her into Coeris, Nikephoros fought him for her and lost, and she has lived since in a widow's house in the village under the castle, writing letters she does not send.

Virtues and Flaws: the Minor Magical Focus in certamen is House Tremere's Virtue. Higher Purpose is the accord; Hatred is Benedek.

Longevity: her own ritual of 1140, renewed in 1195 (Aging modifier -7). She looks sixty.

Twilight scars (Warping 4): doors stand open for her a moment before she reaches them, and close behind her.

characters.summary: A Hungarian maga from Coeris, the covenant's warden and the author of its accord. Severe and orderly, she held the five together for most of a century and took the breaking hardest. She left in the spring of 1212.
characters.secrets:
Coeris sent her. Her former parens, Benedek of Tremere, pressed her for decades for what Dammërstein was hiding, and the pressure was one of the things that broke the accord. Their letters may still be in her sealed quarters.

The truth. In the spring of 1212 Kyrillos, the last one left, told her "Go, then", and that was invitation enough to let her out of the house. She rode home to Coeris. Benedek would not invite her in until she brought what Dammërstein hides, and she would not, because she keeps her word even to a broken accord. She has lived since in the village under the castle, in the one house that ever asked her in, a widow's, and she has not crossed another threshold in eight years.

"Coeris has never seen her" is true of the castle. "Went home and said nothing" is the Tribunal's garbled version. The Echoing Halls rumour is false.

Why the valley's wards lapsed in 1213: they were Ring wards, which last until their circle is broken, and in the spring of 1213 the flood took the stone sill where the line crosses the Schattenbach. She was outside Coeris by then, and no one at the Stone House has invited her back to mend it. An invitation has to be given. A letter from the new council, worded as an invitation home, would bring her. A Ring lasts until its line is broken, so the contest was to break the line. Its rule, agreed between the two of them alone: every seven years she drew the circle anew, and he had until the year's end to find and break it (The Breaking of Wards, and its jokes). Every time she rebuilt them stronger, which meant harder to find and harder to break: the furrow set with stones, hardened with Seal the Earth and Unyielding Earth. Kohlergrund's protection was the product of thirteen such contests, 1122 to 1206, the best warding in the Black Forest because he never let it rest. It ended when they both left.

They are the only two Founders who learned each other's marks. She noticed first, when a man who had lied to her charmingly for eighty years suddenly could not. He worked hers out by testing her thresholds, as he tested everything of hers. Neither told anyone: the one secret they kept for each other, against the accord's clause What the house finds.

He thinks she is still outside Coeris, and the Axis Magica is the contest he has set himself so as not to think about the one he lost. If he comes north for allies, the first thing he will do is test the Stone House's wards, to see whether she is back. Bringing them together again is a story the covenant could give them.

characters.name: Hildegund of Merinita

description.physical_description: A small, quick woman who looks fifty, with a weathered forester's face and laughing grey eyes. Her long hair turns to grey thread at the ends. She dresses in undyed wool and goes barefoot in the forest.
description.biography:
Born in 1094 at the forest's edge above Freiburg, a forester's daughter who played with children nobody else could see (Faerie Upbringing). A Merinita of the Rhine took her as an apprentice, and she passed her Gauntlet in 1113, two years before she came north with the others. She was the youngest of the five. She chose the spur above the Schattenbach for its faerie neighbours, and in the summer of 1115 she went down into the Hollow and made the Stone House's peace with the Spinner's people. That autumn the first skein was paid for.

For ninety years she was the house's door to the forest's other half. She danced at the King Fir's midsummer court and was given a guest-gift she never called in (Faerie Friend). She was Initiated into Glamour, and later into Becoming, whose ordeal left iron burning her hand (Lesser Malediction). She wrote four books, all in the covenant's library: The Spinner's Folk, The Forest Beyond the Road, Bargains with the Spinner and The Silk That Remembers. From 1172 a girl of the valley, Agathe, followed her through the forest, and she let her.

In 1180 she brokered the great skein for Matthaios and the Binding Oath that came with it, and sent Agathe down the Well with the forfeit's words. When the pact lapsed in 1200 the oath marked her: she heard the Wheel every night. In the autumn of 1211, after the last quarrel, she left her talisman in the chapel, asked Agathe to keep leaving the milk, and went down to pay.

Longevity: her own ritual of 1140, renewed in 1190 (Aging modifier -8). She is 117 by her own reckoning; the calendar makes her 126.

Virtues and Flaws: Faerie Magic is House Merinita's Virtue. Glamour and Becoming are Mysteries she was Initiated into (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults), outside the Virtue balance. Compulsion (the Wheel) is her mark from the Binding Oath, also outside the balance; it ended when she paid.

Twilight scars (Warping 8): her hair turns to grey thread at the ends; her shadow moves a little out of step with her, in time with something larger in the webs.

Talisman: the Silver Spindle (Enchanted Items), left in the manor's chapel.

characters.summary: A Swabian, born on the forest's edge, who chose the site for its faerie neighbours and made the covenant's peace with the Spinner's people. Warm, wild and changeable. She left in the autumn of 1211.
characters.secrets:
The truth. In the autumn of 1211 she walked into the Hollow to pay the pact's forfeit, and she sits on the second stool at the Wheel, spinning beside the Spinner. She thinks it is still that autumn. She is the surety for the arrears, about eighty secrets, and stays until they are paid (the Court's page; Settling the arrears in the covenant's secrets).

On the way down she bargained three favours for the house in return for going willingly. The first two were struck in full and the house can call them in. The third, the 90, was never finished, because she sat down at the Wheel before its price was named. Only she can finish it.

Before she went she left her talisman, the silver spindle, on the altar step of the manor's chapel, where no faerie will tread. Spun at the Wheel, it wakes her to herself: she knows the year and what she is. It does not free her.

The clock: the Spinner is filling a hoard of encased silk to change her role, and she needs Hildegund's hands to shape it. When the hoard reaches 40 pawns (the Spinner's hoard, on the Hollow's Triggers; about 1228), Hildegund becomes a thread of the new story and is lost to the house.

She ages only as she lives. At the Wheel she has lived an evening, so she is still 117 by her own reckoning, though the calendar makes her 126.

Each Founder took a Flaw from the Binding Oath for letting the pact lapse in 1200, and each hid it from the others. Hers was the Wheel: from the winter of 1200 she heard it humming every night (Compulsion, Major). She held out for eleven years, until the others had gone, then went down. It ended when she paid, which is why she, and no one else, became the forfeit.

What the valley says (rumours, none confirmed): that she walked into the Spinner's Hollow and did not come out; that the faeries say she is the Spinner's guest, and will come back when the story is finished; that she went to the King of the Black Mountain's court and is held there.

One of The Founders of Dammërstein: the faction card, under The Region, Factions, has the five's accord, Diary, marks and fates together.

links.note: Her oldest friend among the Founders

characters.name: Benedek of Tremere
characters.summary: An elder of Coeris, kept alive past all reason by his longevity ritual, who trained Ilona of Tremere. He rarely leaves his tower and answers letters from everywhere.
characters.secrets:
For decades he pressed Ilona to send Coeris what Dammërstein was hiding. She never did. He has not forgotten the place, and the letters between them are in her sealed quarters.

In the summer of 1212 Nikephoros of Tytalus rode into Coeris and challenged him to certamen for hounding Ilona. The wager was his letters to her, and his promise to leave her be. Benedek won, easily and in front of witnesses. He has kept the letters' memory and the grudge, and the Tribunal story that Nikephoros died that day is one he has never troubled to correct.

Tremere's House Virtue is a Minor Magical Focus in certamen, which is why he beat Nikephoros easily. Ilona has been living outside his gate since 1212; he will invite her in when she brings what Dammërstein hides, and not before.

characters.name: Mother Agathe

description.biography:
A wise woman, not a coven witch: she has no Folk Witch Virtue, no coven and no Witch Moon (Hedge Magic Revised). Second Sight and Premonitions are the Spinner's permanent grants of 1180 (Realms of Power: Faerie, Grant (Minor Virtue)), outside the Virtue balance; Common Sense and Puissant Chirurgy are her own, against Dutybound (the old rules) and Driven (to bring Hildegund home).

Second Sight lets her see the Spinner's people, glamour, and the way into the Hollow's levels. Premonitions is why she knows your business before you say it.

A Binding Thread holds the pact's forfeit in her: when she tries to speak it, her tongue goes still (roll on The thread pulls). Iron shears at the Wheel would cut it.

She carries a copper pot, a bone knife (never iron near the Hollow), and a crock of milk.

characters.summary:
A widow of sixty in a turf-roofed cottage at the head of the valley, who sets bones, brings babies and knows which mushrooms are kind. She talks to the baron's men as if they were her grandsons, and they let her be. Every midsummer she climbs to the Hochtannen with a copper pot, and the baron sells what she gathers to the apothecaries of Strassburg.

She talks to the baron's men as if they were her grandsons, and they let her be. Every midsummer she climbs to the Hochtannen with a copper pot, and the baron sells what she gathers to the apothecaries of Strassburg.

Wants: The Hochtannen left standing; Hildegund home; her tongue free; to be let alone

Offers: Bone-setting, midwifery, herb-craft; the resin, gathered by the rule, for one pawn in three
characters.secrets:
Her history, the forfeit and her debts are on her Neighbours card.

As a girl she followed Hildegund through the forest and learned a little: how to speak to the Spinner's people, and how to take the resin without angering the trees. She is no coven witch: her two Supernatural Virtues, Second Sight and Premonitions, were the Spinner's payment. In 1180, when she was twenty, Hildegund sent her down to the Whispering Well to pay the covenant's price: the real price of the Founders' pact, which was never only one secret a year. Hildegund trusted it to her, and she whispered it to the Spinner. It was spun into thread, and she has not been able to speak it since; when she tries, her tongue goes still. She thinks the Stone House owes her for forty years of silence, and she may be right. She still leaves milk at the Hollow's edge, and she knows the old rules: no iron below, drink from the cup, never thank her.

The real price of the pact was its forfeit, sworn under Binding Oath: if the Stone House ever stops paying, one who built it comes down to the Wheel and stays until the debt is paid. Hildegund trusted the words to Agathe in 1180 so that someone outside the house would carry them, and Agathe whispered them down the Well. The Spinner spun them, and Agathe has not been able to speak them since.

The grants are permanent. The Spinner made them so in 1180, at a cost of 10 points of her Might Score, which she has long since won back. She has no hold on them now, and Agathe knows it. Agathe keeps the old rules out of courtesy and good sense, not because she must. Forty years of use have made her sight keen and her forebodings sure.

Iron shears would cut her thread at the Wheel and let her speak at last. Doing it beneath the Hollow would be an insult the Spinner would not forget. Agathe knows this and has never asked.

The resin. She will gather it for the Stone House, as she did for Hildegund, if it asks her properly, and keep one pawn in three for her remedies and her trouble. She is the only one living who knows the grove's rule: by hand, never iron, never cut the bark, and leave a little behind. The baron's leave was never his to give; she knows that too, and has kept quiet for Gertrud's sake.

reasons.what: Hildegund was kind to her as a girl, and taught her the forest's courtesies.
Forty years of silence for the Stone House, and never once thanked.
New faces at the Stone House, who might bring Hildegund home.

favours.what: She carried the pact's price down the Well for the Founders, and has kept it at the cost of her voice

characters.name: Wolfram von Schattenbach

description.biography:
Landed Noble and Knight, made Poor by his debts (Lords of Men: a Poor Landed Noble has no surplus income, keeps no knights, and has one free season a year). Two manors, as Lords of Men gives a lord of the manor: one for himself and one for which he owes knight service.

Oath of Fealty: sworn to the Zähringen duke, now dead. The oath passes with the duke's rights, so whoever confirms his fiefs can call on him; he hasn't thought that through.

Driven: to be free of Kalb. Wrathful: a carter who argues loses a wheel, and one who argues twice loses more.

Arms: an old sword (Puissant Single Weapon), a heater shield, a mail hauberk past its best, and a hard little Swabian horse.

His one soft place is Gertrud, who is four, and Mother Agathe who kept her alive.

characters.summary:
A Swabian knight of forty with a scarred jaw, two poor manors, a damp keep, a dozen hard men and debts in Strassburg he can't pay. He is no great lord and knows it, and it has made him cruel. The carters call him the robber baron, and the valley has kept the baron. His men chain the Schattenbach at the narrows below his keep and take a bridge-penny from every raft and cart, though there is no bridge. Carters who argue lose a wheel; those who argue twice lose more.

He fells the old firs of the valley and rafts them down the Kinzig to the Rhine, and he calls the whole valley his forest, whatever the charters say.
characters.secrets: His history, claims and debts are on his Neighbours card.

characters.name: Jörg the Fiddler

description.biography:
Born 1137; he looks and feels 25. He ages by the time he lives through (Realms of Power: Faerie), about a season since 1162, so leaving the Hollow doesn't wither him.

Warping 3 from fifty-eight years in the story: he is on the way to becoming a faerie.

True Love: Liese, who has been dead since 1190. He doesn't know.

His fiddle is fir wood strung with grey silk.

characters.summary:
A fair young man in a charcoal-burner's smock sits on a root in the silk hall under the Well, playing a fiddle of fir wood strung with grey silk. The tunes are Kohlergrund tunes, though no one in Kohlergrund has played them for a lifetime. He's cheerful, courteous and glad of company. He'll tell you he's been here "a season, maybe two". Before you leave he always asks, a little anxiously, whether Liese is well.

characters.secrets:
His bargain, his time and Liese's secret are on his Neighbours card.

A mortal kept too long. He came down in 1162 to buy his wife's secret, the one thing Liese had always held back from him, and he has been paying for it in music ever since. Kohlergrund still sings a song about the fiddler who went to the webs and didn't come home.

The Spinner keeps him because he plays beautifully and makes her laugh, and because one day Liese's secret may come to her, and with it a thread straight into the King's line.

The Spinner can't steal a secret, so she couldn't sell Jörg one she didn't have. In 1162 they struck a bargain instead: he plays for her a year and a day, and she tells him Liese's secret the moment it comes to her. It never came, because Liese never went down. His year was paid long ago, and she still owes him an answer she doesn't have; so he waits, sure it has been a season, maybe two. Her first law would also let him go the moment he asked plainly. No one has told him he could.

Time: he does not wither when he leaves. Realms of Power: Faerie has humans in faerie places age by the time they live through, not the years outside, and he has lived through a season or two. What fifty-eight years of glamour have done is begun to make him a faerie (Living in the Story): he has a Warping Score of 3, he forgets, and the Hollow feels more like home than Kohlergrund would. He half-remembers a tune that stops the wheel: the last verse of the song Liese made about him, which he has never heard.

Liese was the King Fir's daughter. About 1140 a burner's wife of Kohlergrund came home from the high firs with a child that wasn't her husband's. Liese grew up fair, quick and a little uncanny, married Jörg the Fiddler, and never told him: that was the one thing she always held back.
