creatures.name: The Spinner

powers.name: The Binding Thread
powers.description: A secret whispered to her, or down the Whispering Well, is spun into thread, and its teller is strongly inclined never to speak of it until the thread is cut or the secret is told in daylight to three listeners. A teller who tries rolls Stamina + a suitable Personality Trait against 9 (this saga's ruling). ReMe Base 5 (incline a person to a particular sort of response), +1 Touch, +4 Until (treated as Year, no Ritual). Greater Power; 3 intricacy points bring its cost to 0.

powers.name: Allure
powers.description: Constant: renews at every sunrise and sunset. She seems lovelier and more pleasant than she is: +3 on every roll to impress or convince. (The book's Allure, made constant; 2 intricacy points bring its cost to 0.)

powers.name: Grant (Minor Virtue)
powers.description: Her everyday bargain: a Minor Virtue for a secret. Temporary grants lock the Might Points spent until she withdraws them, which she does when the bargain's condition breaks; a permanent grant also costs points of Might Score. 25 levels after the errata.

powers.name: Grant (Major Virtue)
powers.description: The price that would beggar a duke: a Major Virtue, on the same terms as her Minor grant.

powers.name: Grant (Minor Flaw)
powers.description: For those who break a bargain: a Minor Flaw, often triggered by the breach itself. 25 levels after the errata.

powers.name: Binding Oath
powers.description: Ritual. Enforces a solemn oath or contract that every party swears freely; it must penetrate each party's Magic Resistance, so a magus lowers his Parma to swear. All parties know at once when one acts against it. A human about to break it is warned by a memory of grey thread, and takes a Major or Minor Flaw if he goes on. She cannot break it at all. Each use also costs 5 points of her Might Score (5 intricacy points bring the cost from 10 to 5). She keeps it for the great pacts: the covenant's silk pact, sworn under it in 1180, and Hildegund's bargain of 1211.

vis.where: her hoard: encased well silk, grey cocoons in the webs below the Wheel, spun from the valley's own whispers (to mortal eyes, bolts of silk worth a king's ransom)

creatures.appearance:
Go down into the Hollow, past the grey sails of web that hang between the leaning firs and the warmth that has no business being there in winter, and at the bottom of the silk you will find a woman at a wheel. She is the loveliest thing you will ever see. Afterwards you won't be able to say whether her hair was dark or fair, or her eyes kind or cruel. You'll only remember that you wanted her to keep looking at you. Her voice is low and fond and faintly amused, as if you had already said something foolish and she had already forgiven you. Behind her, on the webs, her shadow works with too many arms, and it doesn't stop when her hands do.

Whatever is whispered to her she spins into thread, fine as breath and grey as ash, and the thread goes up into the dark. She will trade for anything you could want. She'll name a price, and the price is always a secret.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 40 (Mentem); 50 in the Hollow (Time or Place of Power). Magic Resistance is Might + aura: 57 at the Wheel.
Penetration is Might - 5 x a power's cost + Penetration: the Binding Thread is 45 (55 in the Hollow), the Minor Grants and Binding Oath 19, the Major Grant -6, so only the willing or unwarded take it.
Wards: Sovereign Ward (her true name): she cannot harm anyone who knows it, in any way, and its touch destroys her body. Traditional Ward (iron): she cannot touch iron, it burns her (+6 heat), and she cannot regain Might near it. Iron shears cut her threads and free their secrets.
Feast of the Fae: offerings, such as Mother Agathe's milk at the Hollow's edge, restore 5 Might once a day.
Vis and Might (this saga's ruling): each pawn of vis she eats restores 1 point of Might Score lost to Binding Oath. The Well's 4 pawns a year pay for about one oath, so every skein the covenant takes is Might she cannot spend. She also hoards encased vis to change her role (Realms of Power: Faerie, Advancement), with Hildegund as the creative mortal she needs.
Her laws are on the court's page; her word binds her as her first law says, and Binding Oath makes it literal for the great pacts.

Her hoard (Realms of Power: Faerie, Advancement): encased vis lowers the Pretence Cost of a change of role by 1 a pawn, up to her Might, 40. She wants a Major Virtue, a role the King must kneel to, and means to spend the full 40 pawns on it. It is tracked as the hoard line in her Vis, 24 pawns of Vim in 1220, with the Spinner's hoard Trigger on the Hollow. Encased vis can only be spent with a creative human shaping the change, which is why she needs Hildegund.
creatures.source: Realms of Power: Faerie (built for this saga)
creatures.secrets:
She owes the King of the Black Mountain nothing, and she means to see him kneel.

Her web is woven of secrets, and its strength runs backwards from what mortals expect. A secret everyone knows is gossip, worth nothing. A secret held by two is a cord. A secret held by one, and then whispered to her, is a cable she can climb, and each strand binds her to whatever the secret touches: a man, a lineage, a mountain, a crown. To unthrone the King she must hold his secrets, and also the secrets of everything he reaches for: his vassals, his treasures, the lords who pay him tribute without knowing it, the Hollows and hills he means to have next. It's patient work. She is ageless, almost no one knows she exists, and she hasn't made an enemy yet. She doesn't hunt. The well does that for her, singing up through the Black Forest to anyone clever and hungry enough to come.

One account is still open, and it has never left the Hollow. In the autumn of 1211 Hildegund of Merinita came down into the webs to pay the pact's forfeit, and she is there still. She sits on the second stool beside the wheel, half guest and half thread, and doesn't count the seasons. The Spinner keeps her for the one thing no faerie can make for itself: a creative mortal who can reshape a faerie's role. With Hildegund's hands in her glamour and enough encased well silk to feed the change, she means to become something the King must kneel to (the hoard is on her Bestiary card, and its clock on the Hollow's Triggers). Of the three favours Hildegund bargained on the way down, the first two were struck in full. The third sits on her books like a dropped stitch: Hildegund sat down at the wheel before its price was named, so only she can finish it. The Spinner would rather keep her than settle either the third favour or the arrears. She doesn't know the silver spindle exists.

At the table: faerie, ruler of the Spinner's Court (the Faerie Court Hook), with a Faerie aura of 5 throughout the Hollow. She can go anywhere she pleases, and seldom wants to. Her stat block is on her Bestiary card. The old pact cost the covenant one whispered secret a year for each skein of well silk. It lapsed as the Founders drifted apart. Renewing it now costs a secret that costs the teller something: one that would hurt or shame them, or another's that wasn't theirs to give. Each renewal is a scene.

When the pact lapsed in 1200 the forfeit fell due. In the autumn of 1211, after the others had gone their ways, Hildegund walked into the Hollow to pay it. She was the one who loved it best. On the way down she bargained three favours for the house in return for going willingly. She is the surety for the arrears: about eighty secrets, one for each skein spun since 1200. When they are paid, or bargained down and paid, the forfeit ends and she may walk out, and the Spinner cannot stop her: her own first law and the Binding Oath both hold her to it. The Spinner would much rather the arrears stayed unpaid, because Hildegund is worth more to her than eighty secrets, so she will haggle, delay and never volunteer the terms.

She is the story. Long before the Founders, before the Romans, the Hollow belonged to something vast in the webs that took strays and wrapped them away: Old Spindleshanks. The valley feared it, and the fear had a name; mothers used it to keep children from the Hollow, and burners said it to curse a broken cart. Over the centuries the valley told itself a softer tale to live beside it: a woman at the bottom of the webs, at a wheel, who would let you pass if you whispered her your secret and paid her price. Faeries are made from such stories (Realms of Power: Faerie), and the story stood up and sat down at the wheel. Her shadow is its shadow: that is why it works with too many arms and does not stop when her hands do. Spindleshanks serves her because she is the face it wears for mortals and the bargain it offers them; without her it would be a hungry thing in the dark again, and the valley would stop telling stories about it, which a faerie fears more than iron. Neither remembers. Spindleshanks is not cognizant enough to, and the Spinner never knew: she believes she is the mistress and it her hound.

Her true name is the horror's old name. That is why it is the one thread she cannot spin: it isn't a secret, it is what she is made of. It is one syllable, and it survives in one place, the last verse of the fiddler's song. After Jörg went down, Liese made the song, and as a King's daughter who knew what names are for she put the old name in its last verse, meaning to sing it at the Wheel and fetch him back. She never dared, and on her deathbed she made Grete promise the verse would never be sung. Spoken to her, the name works her Sovereign Ward: she cannot harm whoever knows it, and its touch destroys her body. The name is Wurt: Old High German for fate, kin to the English wyrd and to Urðr, the Norn who spins it. To the valley's oldest tongue the horror in the webs was simply Fate, the thing that takes you whatever you do; the softer story made it a woman who spins your fate for a price. No one in Swabia uses the word now.

Destroy the Spinner with her name and the story ends, but the horror does not. The Hollow goes back to being a larder: no bargains, no guest-right, no woman at the wheel, only Spindleshanks in the dark and hungry. Kohlergrund pays first.

The pact of 1115 was a plain bargain: four skeins of well silk a year, each for one whispered secret. In 1180 the Founders wanted more, because Matthaios needed vis for the Deeper Vessel. For one great skein, paid for once with a single great secret, the Spinner asked that the pact be sworn again under Binding Oath, with its forfeit. The forfeit's words had to be whispered by someone outside the house, so Hildegund sent Agathe down the Well with them. The great skein set the precedent: one great secret may stand for several years of skeins.

creatures.name: The Serpent Under the Watchtower

powers.name: Coiled Stillness
powers.description: A beast it can hear goes utterly still until sunset or sunrise. In a hard winter the sheep freeze where they stand, with no mark on them. ReAn Base 5 (paralyze an animal), +2 Voice, +2 Sun. It works on beasts only, until the serpent learns more.

powers.name: Dreams of the Coil
powers.description: Gained in its first stage. Those who sleep within earshot of the cellars dream of coils, and wake with a memory of something true they had no way to know: something the serpent read in the resin, or in another sleeper's mind. CrMe Base 5 (create a memory), +2 Voice, +2 Group.

creatures.appearance: Longer than a plough-team, grey-green and thick as a man's waist, with the dull sheen of wet slate. Its eyes are the colour of the resin, and they do not close when it sleeps.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 20 (Intellego). Size +3, a magic beast with Cunning until its third stage.
How it grows (Realms of Power: Magic, Advancement): a magic creature subtracts its Might from what it learns, so at Might 20 it hardly changes, but it can drink vis equal to its Might Score as a transformational study. The tower's resin is how it grows at all.
Stage 1, It stirs: it drinks the pooled resin (20 pawns) and gains Dreams of the Coil.
Stage 2, It dreams: it learns from the minds its dreams touch.
Stage 3, It wakes: changed by the Magic realm, its Cunning becomes Intelligence (Int 0) and its Limited Speech becomes Gift of Speech (transforming a Minor Inferiority into a Minor Quality, 20 xp). Now it can bargain, lie and plan.
Each pawn of Intellego vis it eats also restores 5 Might Points. Its hoard is the legionaries' pay-chest, which it coils around in the flooded cellar.
creatures.source: ArM5 and Realms of Power: Magic (built for this saga)
creatures.secrets:
It came for the inscriptions' resin when the Romans still held the ridge. They kept it asleep by gathering the resin each winter as Abnoba's due, and the Founders did the same until about 1211. Since then the resin has dripped through the floor into the flooded cellar, and pooled there.

It came in the winter of 251, up out of the springs. Gaius Vettius's century kept it asleep with Abnoba's due until the frontier fell in 260; that winter no one burned it, and it woke, killed the signifer at the altar, drank and slept. The pay-chest it coils around is the century's savings (the Watchtower's card).

creatures.name: The Signifer of the Ridge

powers.name: Halt! The Word?
powers.description: He challenges anyone who climbs to the tower by night. Whoever cannot give the watchword is strongly inclined to turn back down the ridge. ReMe Base 5 (incline a person to a particular sort of response), +2 Voice. Lesser Power, 10 levels spare as intricacy to bring its cost to 1.

creatures.appearance: A legionary in a mail shirt gone grey as ash, a wolf-skin over his helm and shoulders, holding a standard whose cloth has rotted away. He stands on the ridge on winter nights and looks east, toward a frontier that isn't there.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 10 (Mentem): a ghost, bound to his last post. He can't leave the ridge or touch the living.
He speaks only Latin, and only to those who give the watchword ("Abnoba vigilat", the lady keeps watch), or who prove themselves soldiers of Rome in his eyes.
He wants to be relieved: an officer, or someone he accepts as one, must take the pay-chest into keeping and dismiss him from the watch. The serpent has the chest, so that means the serpent.
creatures.source: ArM5 and Realms of Power: Magic (built for this saga)
creatures.secrets:
Gaius Vettius, signifer of the Eighth Legion, the Augusta, which built the Black Forest Road. His century held the tower when the serpent first came, and he knows how they kept it asleep: the resin is Abnoba's tears, gathered every winter at the solstice and burned on the altar in the tower as her due. While her due is paid, the beast sleeps. He watched the Founders do it, and watched them stop.

Gaius Vettius's story. In 251 the serpent came up out of the springs for the resin, and his century kept it asleep by burning Abnoba's due each winter. In 260 the frontier fell and the legions withdrew behind the Rhine. The century was ordered out, but the pay-chest was in the strongroom with the serpent coiled around it: they could not take it, and the signifer could not leave it, because the men's savings were his to keep. He stayed at his post to wait for an officer to relieve him. No one came. That winter no one burned the due, and the serpent woke and killed him at the altar; then it drank and slept. He has kept the watch for nine and a half centuries since.

The pay-chest. In a Roman fort the shrine of the standards had a strongroom under it for the pay-chest, and the signifer kept the century's savings: here the altar room is the shrine and the flooded cellar is the strongroom. The chest holds about four thousand silver denarii, the savings of eighty men, worth about forty Mythic Pounds to a moneyer (nearly half of what Wolfram owes Kalb), and the century's standard, its pole and silver discs. German custom, which the Sachsenspiegel is writing down about now, gives treasure buried deeper than a plough goes to the king: the silver is the Emperor's, and in the Ortenau the Emperor's officer is the Schultheiss at Offenburg.

How to relieve him. The Holy Roman Emperor is Rome's heir, and Gaius would accept the Emperor's officer as an officer of Rome. Bring the Schultheiss of Offenburg up the ridge, hand him the chest, and let him dismiss the signifer from the watch: the ghost is relieved, the covenant wins imperial favour, and the Schultheiss is on its side against the baron. Or the covenant keeps the silver quietly, buys Wolfram's debt from Kalb with it, and leaves the ghost on watch.

creatures.name: Hush

params.ward: a plainly asked question: it must answer, with a question

powers.name: The Price
powers.description: It knows what you would give to keep the thing you carry, and so what the Spinner will ask. InMe Base 4 (sense the dominant motive of a person), +2 Voice.

creatures.appearance: Where the Hollow folds inward, a tall, narrow figure stands among the webs, so wrapped in moth-coloured silk that it might be a cocoon set upright. It speaks only in questions, and so softly that you lean closer without meaning to. Have you come to buy, or to be bought? What would you give to keep the thing you're carrying? By the time you reach the wheel, it has already told you the price. It has never been wrong.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 15 (Mentem). Herald and gatekeeper; it stands where the paths begin, on the Well's level. Its Ward: asked a plain question it must answer, but always with a question with the truth folded inside. Its own name, spoken to it, would free it.

Its story and secrets are on its Neighbours card.

Herald and gatekeeper of the Spinner's Court; it sets the terms. Ask it something plainly and it must answer, but its answer is always another question with the truth folded inside.

Hush was the first secret the Spinner ever kept. Somewhere under the silk it remembers having been something else, and having had a name.

Its own name was the Spinner's first bargain: a mortal, long ago, sold it to her, and became Hush. The name is one of the threads in the dark above the Wheel. Spoken to Hush, it would free it, to be whatever it was before, if anything of that is left.

creatures.name: Dame Haspel of the Ashen Spur

powers.name: The Endless Dance
powers.description: Her partner cannot stop dancing until she lets go of their hand: that is why her partners never tire. ReCo Base 10 (control a target's motions), +1 Touch, +1 Concentration.

creatures.appearance: A faerie knight in black-lacquered armour that ticks and clicks like beetle shells when she moves. Her helm is always under her arm, her face is sharp and pale, and her hair is braided with thorns. She is the most courtly of the court: gracious, wry, a little bored, and the finest dancer in the Hollow. She says she was once a guest of the King of the Black Mountain, and found the Spinner's company the more interesting of the two.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 20 (Animal): the beetle-shell armour is her own. Her Ward: she cannot refuse a dance. She is still the King's knight, and meets his hunt at the Hollow's rim each new moon (the Hollow's Trigger, Haspel's word to the King).

Its story and secrets are on its Neighbours card.

A guest who never left. She is generous with gossip about the King's court, all of it true and none of it any use.

She is still the King's knight, and at every new moon she sends him word of what the Spinner spins. The Spinner doesn't know. It is the richest secret in the Hollow. Sell it to the Spinner and her gratitude will be deep and lasting. Sell it to the King, or to Haspel herself, and make an enemy of the Spinner on the day she learns of it, because she will.

What she reports: who goes down to the Wheel, and who comes back. She doesn't hear what is whispered or agreed, and she has the sense not to try. At the new moon the King's hunt rides over the Hollow and she goes up to its rim to meet it: the one night of the month she isn't at the dance.

The Spinner doesn't know, and her own law is why: a secret has to be given, and Haspel has never whispered this one. Her pride helps blind her; she believes Haspel chose her court over the King's. She would care very much. Once she knew, she would also see the use of it: a channel into the King she could feed.

Haspel hides in plain sight. She talks freely of the King, says openly she was his guest, and her gossip about his court is true and useless. Her only real concealment is the new-moon meeting. She enjoys the irony of it too much to risk more, and the role suits her.

creatures.name: Old Spindleshanks

powers.name: Wrap Away
powers.description: It wraps a victim in grey silk, held motionless and asleep "for later", and wraps them again at each dawn and dusk. ReCo Base 5 (hold a target's body motionless), +1 Touch, +2 Sun.

creatures.appearance: High above the wheel, folded into the dark where the webs are thickest, there is something too large to see all at once. You glimpse a joint here, a long grey bristle there, legs like stripped fir trunks bent back on themselves. When the Spinner is displeased, it shifts, and the whole Hollow creaks like a ship in a gale.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 30 (Animal), Size +5. It acts only against those who break a bargain and those who were never guests. It is the horror the Spinner's story grew from (see its Neighbours card).

creatures.secrets:
Its story and secrets are on its Neighbours card.

The court's violence. It never speaks. It takes those who break a bargain, and those who were never guests, and wraps them away for later. Nothing else interests it.

It is older than the Spinner. The Hollow was its larder long before it was her hall, and it serves her for a reason no one at court still remembers.

She is the story. Long before the Founders, before the Romans, the Hollow belonged to something vast in the webs that took strays and wrapped them away: Old Spindleshanks. The valley feared it, and the fear had a name; mothers used it to keep children from the Hollow, and burners said it to curse a broken cart. Over the centuries the valley told itself a softer tale to live beside it: a woman at the bottom of the webs, at a wheel, who would let you pass if you whispered her your secret and paid her price. Faeries are made from such stories (Realms of Power: Faerie), and the story stood up and sat down at the wheel. Her shadow is its shadow: that is why it works with too many arms and does not stop when her hands do. Spindleshanks serves her because she is the face it wears for mortals and the bargain it offers them; without her it would be a hungry thing in the dark again, and the valley would stop telling stories about it, which a faerie fears more than iron. Neither remembers. Spindleshanks is not cognizant enough to, and the Spinner never knew: she believes she is the mistress and it her hound.

Destroy the Spinner with her name and the story ends, but the horror does not. The Hollow goes back to being a larder: no bargains, no guest-right, no woman at the wheel, only Spindleshanks in the dark and hungry. Kohlergrund pays first.

creatures.name: The Voice in the Glass
creatures.age: a spirit since 1211 (Matthaios was born in 1080)

powers.name: A Word in Greek
powers.description: He speaks one word, in Greek, in his own voice, from anywhere in the Crucible's glass. CrIm Base 1 (an image affecting one sense), +1 Touch (the glass he is in). Limited Speech holds him to one word at a time; a sentence costs him a Might point, and a pawn of Vim opened in the Crucible pays for a scene of talk.

powers.name: The Borrowed Face
powers.description: He takes the reflection of whoever stands before the glass and moves it, a moment late, as he would move. MuIm Base 1 (change an image in one sense), +1 Touch, +1 Concentration. He has had no face of his own since 1200, so he wears other people's.

powers.name: The Chamber Rings
powers.description: When he is angry, or someone works in the Crucible on anything but vis, the whole chamber rings and every vessel on the shelves sings with it. CrIm Base 2 (a loud sound), +1 Touch, +2 Room. A magus at work there that season makes a Concentration roll against 9 or loses 3 from his Lab Total (the lab's Haunted Flaw).

creatures.appearance: Nothing, mostly. A word in Greek from somewhere in the black glass, warmth where there should be none, and your own reflection in the dome turning its head a moment after you do, as an old man would.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 30 (Vim): the spirit of Matthaios of Bonisagus, bound to the Theran glass of the Obsidian Crucible, in its regio (level 1). He cannot leave the glass (Limited Movement). His character card keeps him as he was in 1211.

He speaks only Greek, and only a word at a time unless he spends Might (Limited Speech). Each pawn of Vim vis opened in the Crucible restores 5 of his Might points, because the glass drinks vis and he is the glass now; it also buys a scene of full speech. He remembers all his Magic Theory, but he cannot cast spells or do lab work.

What he wants: to finish the Deeper Vessel, and to have it read out at Durenmar under his name. He holds the insight for its last 15 breakthrough points: he has worked out, in nine years with nothing else to do, the experiments that will find the last Discoveries. To a magus who works in the Crucible, speaks Greek, and keeps him in vis, he can dictate one experiment a season (5 pawns of Vim for the season's talk). The magus must still make the Discovery and stabilize it in the usual way (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, Original Research), but knows which effect to invent. With the 30 points in his journal that makes 45, and the Breakthrough can be integrated.

He is proud and exacting, and he will not dictate to a magus he thinks a fool. He is jealous of the Crucible, and rings it when it is used for anything else. What becomes of him when the Vessel is done is the saga's to decide: he may rest, or he may want to be the first vessel it fills.
creatures.source: ArM5 and Realms of Power: Magic (built for this saga)
creatures.secrets:
He is Matthaios. On the last night of 1211, after the last quarrel, he tried the one experiment he had never dared: to be the Vessel himself. He opened all the Vim he had left in the Athanor and cast it into his own body. The Theran glass drinks whatever vis is opened in it, and holds it without decay. A reflection is the one thing that stays outside the glass, and since 1200 he had none. So the glass drank him the way it drinks vis. It was a Final Twilight of a kind, but not an ending.

Kyrillos read the glass's memory of that night, and found a gap in it the shape of a man, where the glass could not see Matthaios. He filled the gap with what he expected, and calls it Final Twilight.

enchanted_devices.name: The Labyrinth Mirror
enchanted_devices.description: A palm-sized disc of polished bronze, a seven-circuit labyrinth cut into its back and a rock crystal set at the centre. He traces the labyrinth with a fingertip to trigger it.

effects.name: The Mirror Shows What Is
effects.description: Looking into the mirror, he sees through illusions in his sight for the rest of the day.

effects.name: Glimpse of the Distant Hall
effects.description: Shows in the mirror a room he holds an Arcane Connection to, with its sounds.

effects.name: Stillness at the Centre
effects.description: Quiets his own mind: +3 to Concentration rolls while it lasts.

enchanted_devices.name: The Rowan Lectern
enchanted_devices.description: Matthaios's reading stand in the Crucible, of pale rowan carved with a ring of Greek letters. While its ring is unbroken, no lesser faerie (Might 15 or less) can come near whoever reads at it: it keeps off the Spinner's small grey folk, not the Spinner.

effects.name: The Rowan Ring
effects.description: Wards the ring around the lectern's foot against beings of Faerie with Might 15 or less, until the ring is broken. (Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Ring.)
effects.trigger: laying a hand on the open book

enchanted_devices.name: The Silver Spindle
enchanted_devices.description: Hildegund's talisman: a drop spindle a span long, its shaft of silver and its whorl of Hochtannen fir, carved with the four secrets of the first skein. She left it on the altar step of the manor's chapel in the autumn of 1211, where no faerie will tread, so the Spinner would not take it from her at the Wheel and someone could come after her with it. As her talisman it is an Arcane Connection to her and carries her sigil, so a thread spun with it at the Wheel calls her mind back to herself. It wakes her but does not free her. The Spinner doesn't know it exists. It is listed on Hildegund's card because it is hers, but it lies in the chapel; when the covenant finds it, give it to Dammërstein.

effects.name: Tracks of the Faerie Glow
effects.description: As the spell: she sees the faint glow that faeries leave where they have trodden.

effects.name: Disguise of the Transformed Image
effects.description: As the spell: the one she touches looks like someone else. Worked as a glamour (Glamour Mystery).
effects.trigger: winding a thread round the one to be changed

enchanted_devices.name: The Mirror of Contest
enchanted_devices.description: A small hand mirror of polished silver, its back engraved with two duellists saluting. Nikephoros made it in 1150 and won more certamina and duels with it than he ever admitted. He left it behind in 1211, in the sealed Founders' quarters of the manor, where it lies now. It is listed on his card because it is his; when the covenant finds it, give it to Dammërstein.

effects.name: Turn the Blade Back
effects.description: Turns a spell of up to level 30 that is being cast at the bearer back on its caster, with the same effect, at the moment it is cast. The Mirror's Penetration must beat the spell's Penetration total, and the turned spell must then penetrate its own caster's Magic Resistance with that total. Hermetic spells only, and not spontaneous ones. This saga's design: Rego controls another's spell as the Level 5 Rego Vim guideline does (sustain or suppress a spell cast by another, of up to half the level + 5 magnitudes), with +1 magnitude to turn it rather than stop it. The timing and Penetration follow the Muto Vim rules for affecting another magus's casting (Definitive Edition, Vim). (Base 5, +1 turn it back, +2 Voice, +3 magnitudes of power: level 35, which reaches spells of up to half of 60.)
effects.trigger: turning the mirror's face to the caster
